BURSEVI:v5p342/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p342/r9.claim: مد means stretching or extending, and its noun مدة denotes an extended period; إمداد is often used for desirable things, while مد often appears with harm.
BURSEVI:v5p342/r9.anchor: أصل المد الجر ومنه المدة للوقت الممتد وأكثر ما جاء الإمداد في المحبوب

BURSEVI:v5p342/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p342/r10.claim: The eye is the physical organ, unlike sight; the sacred report says God is the servant's hearing and sight, not ear and eye. The command means not to gaze with desire and inclination.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p372/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p372/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p372/r12.claim: زهرة is read with fatḥa or sukūn on its hāʾ, as نهر is, and can mean attractive bloom, a shining lamp, bright stars, or a tree's blossom.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p372/r12.anchor: زهرة: بفتح الهاء وسكونها نحو نهر ونهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r1.claim: After patience and glorification, Muhammad is told not to prolong his gaze at the worldly goods given to unbelievers, which are temporary like a flower.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r1.anchor: ولما أمره تعالى بالصبر وبالتسبيح جاء النهي عن مد البصر إلى ما متع به الكفرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r2.claim: The warning includes their wealth, children, homes, transport, clothing, and food; the address to the Prophet applies to his community, since he was least attached to worldly adornment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r2.anchor: ولا تعجب يا محمد مما متعناهم به من مال وبنين ومنازل ومراكب وملابس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r3.speaker: رسول الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r3.claim: A Prophetic saying describes the world and its contents as cursed except what is sought for God’s sake.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r3.anchor: وهو القائل في الدنيا «ملعونة ملعون ما فيها إلا ما أريد به وجه الله»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r4.claim: Stretching one’s gaze is stronger than simply looking, since it implies prolonged admiration; a brief involuntary glance is excused.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r4.anchor: ولا تمدن أبلغ من لا تنظر لأن مد البصر يقتضي الإدامة والاستحسان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r5.claim: The pious avert their eyes from the luxury of tyrants and immoral people because the display is meant to attract spectators and their attention encourages its owners.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r5.anchor: فالناظر إليها محصل لغرضهم وكالمغري لهم على اتخاذها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r6.claim: Azwājan is parsed as a direct object, meaning groups of unbelievers, with منهم as its modifier; al-Zamakhshari offers an alternative circumstantial parsing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r6.anchor: وانتصب أزواجا على أنه مفعول به، والمعنى أصنافا من الكفرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows azwājan to be a circumstantial accusative, while taking منهم as the object of bestowed, meaning some groups of people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r7.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري أن ينتصب أزواجا عن الحال من ضمير به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r8.speaker: مكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r8.claim: The word flower has several proposed syntactic roles, including blame, a second object, apposition, predicate, or circumstantial accusative; Makkī prefers the final analysis, while apposition to the pronoun is rejected for separating the verb from its complement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p399/r8.anchor: وزَهرة منصوب على الذم أو مفعول ثان لمتعنا على تضمينه معنى أعطينا

FARRA:v2p196/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p196/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p196/r2.claim: أزواجا منهم means men among them.

FARRA:v2p196/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p196/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p196/r3.claim: زهرة is accusative through متعناهم به; Arabic can place a direct object after a verb even when the noun is definite, as the cited poem demonstrates.
FARRA:v2p196/r3.anchor: نصبت الزهرة على الفعل متعناهم به زهرة فى

MAJAZ:v2p32/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p32/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p32/r6.claim: Zahrat al-ḥayāt al-dunyā means the adornment and beauty of worldly life.
MAJAZ:v2p32/r6.anchor: «زهرة الحياة الدنيا» (131) أي زينة الدنيا وجمالها

MAJAZ:v2p32/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p32/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p32/r7.claim: Linaftinahum means so that We may test them with it.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r10.claim: The Prophet must not gaze beyond an initial glance at the worldly luxuries given to disbelieving groups; those goods are a trial and do not benefit them in the afterlife.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r10.anchor: لا تطول نظرهما بعد النظرة الأولى المعفو عنها قاصدا للاستحسان

BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r11.claim: The Lord's good, sufficient provision is better than disbelievers' adornments because it does not lead to excess and its reward endures; calling it God's provision is honorific and signals its lawful character.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r11.anchor: الكفاف الطيب المقرون بالتوفيق { خير } من زهرتهم

DURR-FULL:v5p611/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r7.speaker: أبو رافع
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r7.claim: When the Prophet lacked food for a guest, he sought flour on credit from a Jewish man, who demanded armor as security; the next verse consoled the Prophet about worldly enjoyment.
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r7.anchor: عن أبي رافع قال: أضاف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيفا ولم يكن عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما يصلحه

DURR-FULL:v5p611/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r8.speaker: سفيان
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r8.claim: Sufyan says the warning against coveting worldly enjoyment is consolation for the Messenger of God.
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r8.anchor: عن سفيان في قوله: {ولا تمدن عينيك} الآية قال: تعزية لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r8.speaker: السخاوي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r8.claim: Al-Itqān reports an exception for 20:130 and considers 20:131 another likely exception from the Meccan classification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r8.anchor: وفي ( الإتقان ) أنه استثني منها آية : { فاصبر على ما يقولون وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r9.speaker: أبو رافع
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r9.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ reports that after a Jewish man refused to lend flour without collateral, the Prophet declared his trustworthiness and 20:131 was revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r9.anchor: لما أخرج أبو يعلى والبزار عن أبي رافع قال : ( أضاف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r10.claim: If Abū Rāfiʿ’s report is sound, Ibn ʿĀshūr thinks it confuses recitation with revelation: he may have heard the Prophet recite a familiar verse and assumed it had just descended.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r10.anchor: وعندي أنه إن صح حديث أبي رافع فهو من اشتباه التلاوة بالنزول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r11.claim: Alternatively, the report may use descent to mean recitation; such confusion recurs in transmitted occasions of revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r11.anchor: أو أطلق النزول على التلاوة . ولهذا نظائر كثيرة في المرويات في أسباب النزول

JISHUMI:v7p4769/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r7.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r7.claim: Yaqub reads زهرة with an open hāʾ; other readers use a still hāʾ, both being dialect forms.
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r7.anchor: قرأ يعقوب: زهرة الحياة بفتح الهاء، والقراء على سكونها، وهما لغتان

JISHUMI:v7p4769/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r10.claim: Imtaʿ means taking pleasure in what one perceives; mattaʿa intensifies the sense of giving enjoyment.
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r10.anchor: الإمتاع: الالتذاذ بما يدرك، أمتعه إمتاعا، ومتعه تمتيعا

JISHUMI:v7p4769/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r11.claim: Azwaj can mean matching counterparts or categories; the original sense of pair is one joined with another.
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r11.anchor: والأزواج: الأشكال، وأصل الزوج في اللغة الواحد الذي يكون معه آخر

MUQATIL:20:130-131/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:130-131/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:130-131/r4.claim: Do not stare at the varied wealth God gave Meccan unbelievers: it is worldly adornment by which they are tested; the garden in the Hereafter is better and more lasting.
MUQATIL:20:130-131/r4.anchor: { ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم } يعنى كفار مكة من الرزق أصنافا منهم من الأموال،

STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r1.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r1.claim: Ṭā Hā is Makkan; some classify verses 130–131 as Madinan, but their context suggests they are Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r1.anchor: which some consider to be Madinan (JJ)

TABATABAI:20:130-131/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r6.claim: “Do not extend your eyes” means do not fix one's gaze on something; extending the gaze is a metonym for attachment to and love of it.
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r6.anchor: مد العين مد نظرها وإطالته ففيه مجاز عقلي ثم مد النظر وإطالته إلى شيء كناية عن التعلق به وحبه

TABATABAI:20:130-131/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r7.claim: “Groups among them” may mean classes of unbelievers or their male and female pairings and households; the indefinite plural minimizes their importance.
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r7.anchor: الأصناف من الكفار أو الأزواج من النساء والرجال

TABATABAI:20:130-131/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r8.claim: “The flower of worldly life” explains what God has granted them: its adornment and brightness; their enjoyment is a test, with some interpreting it as punishment through wealth and children.
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r8.anchor: بمنزلة التفسير لقوله { ما متعنا به }

TABATABAI:20:127-135/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r1.speaker: أبو رافع
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r1.claim: Abu Rafi reports that the Prophet sought flour on credit for a guest and offered his armor as security; the verse was said to console him about worldly life.
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r1.anchor: أضاف النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ضيفا ولم يكن عند النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ما يصلحه فأرسلني إلى رجل من اليهود

TABATABAI:20:127-135/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r2.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects the proposed occasion involving a loan and the Prophet's armor because the verse, especially its conclusion, does not fit that story.
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r2.anchor: ومضمون الآية وخاصة ذيلها لا يلائم القصة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r3.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r3.claim: Mujāhid explains the worldly goods the Prophet must not covet as the wealth of the rich.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r3.anchor: قوله: {ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم} [طه: 131] تفسير مجاهد يعني: الأغنياء.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r4.claim: Qatāda glosses the flower of worldly life as its adornment and says it is given to test its owners; Yaḥyā says God tests them with it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r4.anchor: قال قتادة: زينة الحياة الدنيا. أمره أن يزهد في الدنيا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r5.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r5.claim: A report says a person becomes grateful and patient by modeling the more devout person and the less wealthy one; looking to wealthier people and less devout people has the opposite result.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r5.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن ثوبان قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " خصلتان من كانتا فيه كتبه الله شاكرا صابرا،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r6.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r6.claim: The Prophet asks God to make his household's provision sufficient and says sufficient provision is the best provision.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r6.anchor: نا الحسن بن دينار عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «خير الرزق الكفاف، اللهم اجعل رزق آل محمد كفافا»

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r1.claim: The surah closes with encouragement for the Prophet and believers facing pressure: punishment awaits its divinely set time, so believers should endure, worship steadily, and keep striving; this work benefits them, and a blessed future belongs to the God-conscious.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r1.anchor: müminlerin İslâm mesajının hedefine ulaşması için bu tür beklentilere bel bağlamak yerine karşılaştıkları zorluklara katlanmaları, sürekli bir ibadet bilinci ve disiplini içinde mücadeleye devam etmeleri istenmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r5.claim: The warning recalls that believers might envy unbelievers’ prosperity; worldly comfort does not prove eternal happiness or God’s favor, and life is a test.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r5.anchor: dünya hayatındaki refah düzeyi ebedî mutluluğun ve hele Allah’ın hoşnutluğunun göstergesi değildir; bu hayat bir sınavdan ibarettir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r6.claim: This is not a call to poverty: believers may enjoy lawful goods, help others, withstand deprivation, and find happiness through trust in God and seeking His favor.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r6.anchor: Mümin helâlinden elde ettiği dünya nimetlerinden yararlanır, başkalarına da yardım eder; yokluk ve yoksulluk halinde çökmez

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r7.speaker: Derveze
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r7.claim: Although reports place verses 130–131 in Medina, the author doubts this, especially because their style is Meccan.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r7.anchor: bunların Medine’de indiğine dair rivayeti tereddütle karşılamak gerekir; özellikle üslûp açısından bunların Mekkî âyet özelliği taşıdığı görülmektedir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r1.claim: The Prophet is told not to worry over the wealthy; their refusal is their own deprivation, and God does not need their resources.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r1.anchor: God does not need their wealth and resources.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r2.claim: The worldly resources refer to Quraysh's political elites in Mecca and Ṭāʾif, who offered wealth if the Prophet would stop preaching; his concern for them came from sincere compassion, not greed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r2.anchor: instead of accepting it, he recited before them some verses

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r3.claim: Worldly wealth and resources are God's bestowals, not simply inheritance or personal intelligence, and test whether their recipients are grateful.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r3.anchor: they are God’s bestowal and by it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r4.claim: The expression about worldly life's adornment is a circumstantial accusative; worldly resources are transient and should be used to earn for the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p85/r4.anchor: Such accusative of states are common in eloquent Arabic and many examples of it have been pointed out in this exegesis.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r1.claim: The wealth's brightness soon fades; its proper use is to earn for the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r1.anchor: Its brightness will whither away soon and leave it scarred.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r2.claim: The phrase about testing people with worldly favors refers to God's established practice: hardship tests patience and favor tests gratitude; wealth is a trial, not an entitlement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r2.anchor: When He inflicts them with hardships, the purpose is to test their patience and when He blesses them with favours, the purpose is to test how grateful they are.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r3.claim: The Prophet and his companions need no patronage from ungrateful elites because God's provision will be far better and everlasting, unlike their brief worldly wealth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r3.anchor: It will never fa de away.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r4.claim: Piety grows from the nourishment God revealed; trying to cultivate it with stagnant water is unnatural and yields vice rather than virtue.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r4.anchor: if it seemingly does grow, then it will bear fruits of vice and not virtue.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p147/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p147/r3.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p147/r3.claim: Al-Suyuti proposes excluding another verse, citing Abu Rafi's report: after a Jew refused to lend the Prophet flour without collateral, the verse about not coveting others' worldly provision was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p147/r3.anchor: وقال الجلال السيوطي : ينبغى أن يستثنى آية اخرى فقد أخرج البزار وأبو يعلى عن أبى رافع

RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r1.claim: After consoling the Prophet about what people said and directing him to glorification, God follows with a prohibition against gazing at their worldly allotment.
RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r1.anchor: لما صبر رسوله عليه السلام على ما يقولون

RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r2.claim: One view takes this literally: prolonging the gaze means lingering in admiration without turning away; an ordinary brief glance followed by lowering the eyes is excused.
RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r2.anchor: المراد منه نظر العين وهؤلاء قالوا

RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r3.claim: Rāzī illustrates the temptation with Qarun's spectators wishing for his fortune and the learned believers answering that God's reward is better for believers who act rightly.
RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r3.anchor: كما فعل نظارة قارون حيث قالوا

RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r4.claim: Because gazing at worldly adornment is instinctive, the verse warns against a habitual lingering look; ascetics therefore urged lowering the eyes from tyrants' buildings and the clothes and mounts of the immoral, since spectators advance their display's purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r4.anchor: ولما كان النظر إلى الزخارف كالمركوز في الطباع

RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r5.claim: Abū Muslim says the prohibition concerns grief over what others received in worldly fortune, not looking at it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p116#3/r5.anchor: قال أبو مسلم الذي نهى عنه بقوله

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r1.speaker: أبو رافع
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r1.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ reports that after a guest came, the Prophet sent him to a Jew for a sale or loan; the Jew required collateral, so the Prophet sent his armor, and the verse was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r1.anchor: قال أبو رافع : ( نزل ضيف بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r2.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r2.claim: The Prophet said God does not look at people's forms or wealth, but at their hearts and deeds; Rāzī gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r2.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : ( إن الله لا ينظر إلى صوركم ولا إلى أموالكم

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r3.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ calls the world a home for the homeless and wealth for the wealthless, gathered by those lacking reason.
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r3.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء : الدنيا دار من لا دار له

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r4.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says that without people's foolishness, the world would be ruined.
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r4.anchor: وعن الحسن : لولا حمق الناس لخربت الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r5.speaker: عيسى ابن مريم
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r5.claim: Jesus son of Mary warns people not to take the world as a lord, lest it make them its slaves.
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r5.anchor: وعن عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام قال : لا تتخذوا الدنيا ربا

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r6.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r6.claim: When ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr saw what rulers possessed, he recited this verse and called people to prayer and God's mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r6.anchor: وعن عروة بن الزبير أنه كان إذا رآى ما عند السلاطين

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r7.claim: Rāzī glosses “what We have given them to enjoy” as what We have made delightful: pleasing sights, melodies, scents, clothing, and sexual or marital pleasures.
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r7.anchor: والإمتاع الإلذاذ بما يدرك من المناظر الحسنة ويسمع

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r8.claim: He notes the forms “amtāʿan” and “mattāʿan”; the intensive tفعيل form suggests repeated or abundant enjoyment.
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r8.anchor: يقال أمتعه إمتاعا ومتعه تمتيعا والتفعيل يقتضي التكثير

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r9.claim: Rāzī first explains “groups” as counterparts among the unbelievers: the word derives from pairing and resemblance, since they resemble one another in straying from right judgment.
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r9.anchor: أي أشكالا وأشباها من الكفار وهي من المزاوجة بين الأشياء وهي المشاكلة

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses “azwājan” as classes or kinds of people.
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : أصنافا منهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r11.speaker: الكلبي والزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r11.claim: Al-Kalbī and al-Zajjāj gloss “azwājan” as men.

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r12.claim: Rāzī lists four accusative analyses for “zahra”: blame or specification; a second object if “We gave” is implied; apposition to the prepositional phrase's case; or apposition to “groups” with an implied “possessors of.”

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r13.claim: For the vocalized form, Rāzī gives “zahra” its ordinary sense of adornment and brightness, as in “jahra” in the reading of 2:55.
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r13.anchor: قلنا معنى الزهرة بعينه وهو الزينة والبهجة

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r14.claim: Alternatively, “zahra” may be a plural of “zāhir,” describing the worldly people as bright-faced and radiant, unlike the pale, plainly dressed righteous.
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r14.anchor: وأن يكون جمع زاهر وصفا لهم بأنهم زهرة هذه الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r15.claim: One explanation of the test is punishment through wealth and children, as in the warning that God intends to punish people by them in worldly life.

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the test as God's causing them to go astray.
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r16.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : إضلالا مني لهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r17.speaker: الكبي ومقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r17.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say worldly abundance intensifies obligation: resisting available pleasures is harder, the rich bear duties the poor lack, and those able to sin find abstention harder.
RAZI-FULL:v22p117/r17.anchor: قال الكبي ومقاتل تشديدا في التكاليف عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r1.claim: Rāzī's preferred reading is that the reward the Prophet will receive is better than the unbelievers' worldly gain and endures, unlike their temporary possessions.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r1.anchor: والأظهر أن المراد أن مطلوبك الذي تجده من الثواب

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r2.claim: Another possibility is that even modest worldly provision joined with obedience is better in its outcome and more lasting, if one is content and patient with it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد ما أوتيته من يسير الدنيا إذا قرنته بالطاعة خير لك من حيث العاقبة وأبقى

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r3.claim: A further possibility is that “your Lord's provision” means the prophethood and exalted ranks given to the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد ما أعطى من النبوة والدرجات الرفيعة

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r15.claim: After the counsel on patience and prayer, Rāzī reads the following account of the opponents' objection as continuing the instruction to endure what they say in 20:130.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r15.anchor: ثم إنه سبحانه بعد هذه الوصية حكى عنهم شبهتهم

RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r1.claim: The account of the jinn who listened to the Quran and returned to warn their people explicitly establishes their existence, hearing the revelation and warning others.
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r1.anchor: الآية الأولى قوله تعالى : ^ { وإذ صرفنا إليك نفرا من الجن يستمعون القرآن فلما حضروه قالوا أنصتوا

RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r2.claim: The Quran's statement that devils followed what was recited during Solomon's reign is evidence for their existence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r2.anchor: والآية الثانية قوله تعالى : ^ { واتبعوا ما تتلوا الشياطين على ملك سليمان }

RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r3.claim: The account of devils serving Solomon by making sanctuaries, statues, basins and fixed cauldrons affirms their existence and activity.
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r3.anchor: الآية الثالثة قوله تعالى في قصة سليمان عليه السلام : ^ { يعملون له ما يشاء من محاريب وتماثيل

RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r4.claim: The Quran describes devils as builders, divers and beings bound in chains, furnishing further evidence for their existence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r4.anchor: وقال تعالى : ^ { والشياطين كل بناء وغواص وآخرين مقرنين في الأصفاد } ^ [ ص : ]

RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r5.claim: The Quran says the wind served Solomon and some jinn worked before him by his Lord's permission, affirming the jinn's existence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r5.anchor: وقال تعالى : ^ { ولسليمان الريح } ^ إلى قوله تعالى : ^ { ومن الجن من يعمل بين يديه بإذن ربه }

RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r6.claim: The challenge addressed to jinn and humans to cross the regions of the heavens and earth treats both as real beings.
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r6.anchor: الآية الرابعة قوله تعالى : ^ { يا معشر الجن والإنس إن استطعتم أن تنفذوا من أقطار السموات والأرض }

RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r7.claim: The statement that the lower heaven is adorned with stars and guarded from every rebellious devil attests to devils' existence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r7.anchor: الآية الخامسة قوله تعالى : ^ { إنا زينا السماء الدنيا بزينة الكواكب وحفظا من كل شيطان مارد }

RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r8.claim: Abu Saʿid recounts finding a snake under his bed and tells of a newly married man who speared a snake in his home and died as it did; he reported this to the Prophet, but the excerpt cuts off before the Prophet's response. No grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v1p73/r8.anchor: روى مالك في الموطأ عن صيفي بن أفلح عن أبي السائب مولى هشام بن زهرة أنه دخل على أبي سعيد الخدري

STUDYQURAN:20:131/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:131/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:131/r1.claim: The Prophet is admonished not to covet worldly goods given to the Makkans who reject him.
STUDYQURAN:20:131/r1.anchor: the Prophet is being admonished not to desire the things of the world that have been given to the Makkans who are rejecting him

STUDYQURAN:20:131/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:131/r2.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:20:131/r2.claim: “That We may test them concerning it” means that God will punish them for it in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:20:131/r2.anchor: That We may test them concerning it means “that We may punish them in the Afterlife on account of it” (Z)

STUDYQURAN:20:131/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:131/r3.speaker: Ṭū
STUDYQURAN:20:131/r3.claim: The provision is the Hereafter’s reward promised to the Prophet, better and more enduring than the disbelievers’ worldly enjoyments; the passage parallels God being called better and more lasting.
STUDYQURAN:20:131/r3.anchor: the rewards that God has promised the Prophet in the Hereafter are far better and longer lasting than the enjoyments He has given the disbelievers in this life

STUDYQURAN:20:131/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:131/r4.speaker: Su
STUDYQURAN:20:131/r4.claim: Spiritually, God’s provision refers to trust in Him (tawakkul), more enduring than one’s own efforts to obtain what one wants.

STUDYQURAN:20:131/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:131/r5.speaker: Su
STUDYQURAN:20:131/r5.claim: Alternatively, provision refers to contentment with God together with complete reliance upon Him.
STUDYQURAN:20:131/r5.anchor: Alternatively, provision here could be a reference to both contentment with God and total reliance upon Him (Su)

TAB-FULL:v16p213/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r1.claim: The Prophet is told not to look with longing at worldly enjoyment granted to counterparts of those who turn away from God's signs.
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r1.anchor: يتمتعون بها، من زهرة عاجل الدنيا ونضرتها

TAB-FULL:v16p213/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r2.claim: Their attractive worldly enjoyment is a passing deception and a test by which God tries them.
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r2.anchor: لنختبرهم فيما متعناهم به من ذلك، ونبتليهم

TAB-FULL:v16p213/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r3.claim: The promised afterlife reward from God is better than their worldly adornment and lasts forever without ending or depletion.
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r3.anchor: وأدوم، لأنه لا انقطاع له ولا نفاذ

TAB-FULL:v16p213/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r4.speaker: أبو رافع
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r4.claim: Abu Rafi reports that the Prophet sent him to borrow food from a Jewish man, who demanded collateral; the Prophet was saddened, and the verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r4.anchor: عن أبي رافع، قال: أرسلني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى يهودي يستسلفه، فأبى أن يعطيه إلا برهن، فحزن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v16p213/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r5.speaker: أبو رافع
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r5.claim: In another Abu Rafi report, a Jewish lender required a pledge after a guest arrived; the Prophet offered his armor, and verses 15:87 and 20:131–132 were revealed.
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r5.anchor: عن أبي رافع، قال: نزل برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيف: فأرسلني إلى يهودي بالمدينة يستسلفه، فأتيته

TAB-FULL:v16p215/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p215/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p215/r1.claim: Ṭabarī parses زهرة as accusative, attached to the action of granting enjoyment despite the intervening pronoun in متعنا به.
TAB-FULL:v16p215/r1.anchor: أبعد الذي بالسفح سفح كواكب … رهينة رمس من تراب وجندل

TAB-FULL:v16p215/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p215/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p215/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites a Banū Fuqʿas poem using رهينة as an accusative by an implied verb; Ṭabarī says this is weaker evidence because the noun is governed by a preposition.
TAB-FULL:v16p215/r2.anchor: فنصب رهينة على الفعل من قوله: «أبعد الذي بالسفح»

TAB-FULL:v16p215/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p215/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p215/r3.claim: Qatādah glosses the test as trial and says the Lord's provision is better and more lasting than their worldly enjoyment.

TAB-FULL:v16p217/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p217/r2.speaker: عروة
TAB-FULL:v16p217/r2.claim: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa reports that when ʿUrwa saw the rulers' worldly goods, he went home, recited these verses, and called his family to prayer.
TAB-FULL:v16p217/r2.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، قال: كان عروة إذا رأى ما عند السلاطين دخل داره، فقال

TABATABAI:20:131-132/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r1.claim: The prohibition on admiring worldly wealth and children in 9:85 parallels the warning not to gaze at worldly adornment here.
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r1.anchor: ولا تعجبك أموالهم وأولادهم إنما يريد الله أن يعذبهم بها في الدنيا

TABATABAI:20:131-132/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r2.claim: “Your Lord's provision” means the afterlife provision, better and more enduring than the temporary adornment bestowed on worldly groups as a test.
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r2.anchor: المراد به بقرينة مقابلته لما متعوا به من زهرة الحياة الدنيا هو رزق الآخرة وهو خير وأبقى

TABATABAI:20:131-132/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r3.claim: The verse tells the Prophet not to prolong his gaze at worldly beauty and enjoyment granted to groups of people as a trial; God's afterlife reward is better and lasting.
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r3.anchor: لا تطل النظر إلى زينة الحياة الدنيا وبهجتها التي متعنا بها أصنافا أو أزواجا معدودة منهم لنمتحنهم

TABRISI:20:131/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r1.speaker: يعقوب وسهل
TABRISI:20:131/r1.claim: Yaqub and Sahl read زهرة with fatḥa on the hāʾ; the other readers use sukūn there.
TABRISI:20:131/r1.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب وسهل زهرة بفتح الهاء والباقون بسكونها

TABRISI:20:131/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:131/r3.claim: Zahra means the beauty and brightness of worldly life, something pleasing to the eye.
TABRISI:20:131/r3.anchor: { زهرة الحياة الدنيا } حسنها ويجوز فتح العين فيها والزهرة النور الذي يروق عند الرؤية

TABRISI:20:131/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:131/r4.claim: The description أزهر اللون means a luminous or bright complexion.
TABRISI:20:131/r4.anchor: ومنه الحديث في صفة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان أزهر اللون أي نير اللون

TABRISI:20:131/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:131/r5.claim: Al-Baqara and Al Imran are called the two radiant suras, and Friday is called a radiant day.
TABRISI:20:131/r5.anchor: والزهراوان: البقرة وآل عمران ويوم الجمعة يوم أزهر

TABRISI:20:131/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r6.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:20:131/r6.claim: Zahra is accusative because متعنا means “We made worldly life a flower for them”; the purpose is to make it a trial for them.
TABRISI:20:131/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج: زهرة منصوب بمعنى متعنا لأن معناه جعلنا لهم الحياة الدنيا زهرة لنفتنهم

TABRISI:20:131/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r7.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:20:131/r7.claim: Alternatively, Zahra is a circumstantial accusative referring either to the pronoun in به or to ما متعنا به.
TABRISI:20:131/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون حالا من الهاء في به ويجوز أن يكون حالا من ما متعنا به

TABRISI:20:131/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r10.speaker: أبو رافع
TABRISI:20:131/r10.claim: A guest led the Prophet to ask a Jewish man for flour on credit until Rajab or to borrow it; the man demanded collateral, so the Prophet sent his iron armor and said he would repay. The verse was revealed to console him about worldly goods.
TABRISI:20:131/r10.anchor:
قال أبو رافع:
" نزل برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيف فبعثني إلى يهودي

TABRISI:20:131/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:131/r11.claim: The author says he already explained “do not stretch your eyes” in the commentary on al-Hijr.

TABRISI:20:131/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r12.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TABRISI:20:131/r12.claim: Ubayy says whoever is not consoled by God’s consolation is consumed by regrets; watching others’ possessions prolongs sorrow without satisfying resentment, and measuring blessings only by food and drink diminishes knowledge and hastens punishment.
TABRISI:20:131/r12.anchor: وقال أبي بن كعب: في هذه الآية من لم يتعز بعزاء الله تقطعت نفسه حسرات على الدنيا

TABRISI:20:131/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r13.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:20:131/r13.claim: The author’s companions report that when this verse came down, the Prophet sat upright and repeated the foregoing words of consolation.
TABRISI:20:131/r13.anchor: وروى أصحابنا عن أبي عبد الله ع أنه قال لما نزلت هذه الآية استوى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جالسا

TABRISI:20:131/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
TABRISI:20:131/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada explain زهرة as the adornment of worldly life.
TABRISI:20:131/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة: زينة الحياة الدنيا

TABRISI:20:131/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:131/r15.claim: One explanation is that God tests them by demanding strenuous obedience to truth and payment of the rights due on their wealth.
TABRISI:20:131/r15.anchor: لنعاملهم معاملة المختبر بشدة التعبد في العمل بالحق في هذه الأمور وأداء الحقوق عنه

TABRISI:20:131/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:131/r16.claim: Alternatively, their abundant wealth and the Prophet’s relative poverty make following him and obeying him a heavier religious demand.
TABRISI:20:131/r16.anchor: لنشدد عليهم التعبد بأن نكلفهم متابعتك والطاعة لك مع كثرة أموالهم وقلة مالك

TABRISI:20:131/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:131/r17.claim: Another reading is that God gives some worldly people abundant provision as punishment, since worldly life is insignificant to Him.
TABRISI:20:131/r17.anchor: معناه لنعذبهم به لأن الله قد يوسع الرزق على بعض أهل الدنيا تعذيبا له

TABRISI:20:131/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r18.speaker: ع
TABRISI:20:131/r18.claim: A saying attributed in the source to ع states that if the world weighed even as much as a gnat’s wing to God, He would not give a disbeliever a drink of water.
TABRISI:20:131/r18.anchor: ولذلك قال ع: لو كانت الدنيا تزن عند الله جناح بعوضة ما سقى منها كافرا شربة ماء

TABRISI:20:131/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:131/r19.claim: The provision God promises the Prophet in the afterlife is better than the worldly enjoyment given to these people and more enduring.
TABRISI:20:131/r19.anchor: أي ورزق ربك الذي وعدك به في الآخرة خير مما متعنا به هؤلاء في الدنيا { وأبقى } أي أدوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p559/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p559/r1.speaker: أبو رافع
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p559/r1.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ reports that this verse came after a Jewish seller refused the Prophet’s request to sell and lend until Rajab without collateral; the Prophet offered his armor as security and said he was trustworthy in heaven and earth. No grading is stated.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p559/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {ولا تمدن عينيك} الآية، قال أبو رافع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p559/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p559/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p559/r2.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb glosses azwājan as counterparts among the unbelievers, people alike in turning from what is right.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p559/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {أزواجا منهم} قال أبي بن كعب: (أشباها من الكفار)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p559/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p559/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p559/r3.claim: Ubayy warns that envying others’ worldly possessions brings grief, while seeing blessing only in food and drink diminishes knowledge and brings punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p559/r3.anchor: وقال أبي بن كعب في هذه الآية: (فمن لم يتعز بعزة الله تقطعت نفسه حسرات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddī gloss the world’s bloom as its adornment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {زهرة الحياة الدنيا} قال ابن عباس، والسدي: (زينة الدنيا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r2.claim: The linguists define zahrah as the world’s brightness, freshness, and beauty, deriving it from the eye-catching blossoms of a tree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r2.anchor: وقال أهل اللغة: (زهرة الدنيا بهجتها ونضارتها وحسنها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq parses zahrah in the accusative as the result of what God gave them to enjoy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (و {زهرة} منصوب بمعنى متعنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r4.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r4.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the purpose as testing them; the author explains it as testing their gratitude for what they were given.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r5.claim: Abū Isḥāq says God makes those worldly goods a trial for them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r5.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (لنجعل ذلك فتنة لهم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p561/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the phrase as God’s misguidance of them by letting favor increase their disbelief and transgression; the author says this best fits the unbelievers’ condition and God’s treatment of them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Lord’s provision refers to the resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562/r1.anchor: {ورزق ربك} قال ابن عباس: (يريد: في المعاد)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562/r2.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562/r2.claim: Al-Suddī and others identify the Lord’s provision as Paradise.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562/r3.claim: The provision is greater and more enduring.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:131/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:131/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:131/r1.claim: The explanation of this phrase is given in Surat al-Hijr.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:131/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:131/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:131/r2.claim: The flower of worldly life is its adornment and beauty.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:131/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:131/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:131/r3.claim: God gives them these things as a trial.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:131/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:131/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:131/r4.claim: The provision of the Lord, reserved for the Hereafter, is better and more enduring.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:131/r4.anchor: لك في المعاد { خير وأبقى } أكثر وأدوم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r1.claim: The provision from the Lord refers to provision in Paradise.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r2.claim: That provision is better than the goods of this world.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r3.claim: It lasts without coming to an end.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r4.claim: Qatāda says God's provision is better and more enduring than worldly splendor.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r4.anchor: سعيد عن قتادة قال: {ورزق ربك خير وأبقى} [طه: 131] مما متع به هؤلاء من زهرة الحياة الدنيا.

QASHANI:20:131-133/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:131-133/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:131-133/r1.claim: Extending one's gaze signifies the soul's changing inclinations toward worldly adornments, tests for worldly people.
QASHANI:20:131-133/r1.anchor: { ولا تمدن عينيك } في التلوينات النفسية وظهور النفس بالميل إلى الزخارف الدنيوية

QASHANI:20:131-133/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:131-133/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:131-133/r2.claim: The Lord's provision is afterlife realities, knowledge, and spiritual lights, which are better and more lasting.
QASHANI:20:131-133/r2.anchor: { ورزق ربك } من الحقائق والمعارف الأخروية والأنوار الروحانية { خير وأبقى } أفضل وأدوم

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r1.claim: An unattributed verse depicts disciplining the eye for admiring anyone other than the beloved; Qushayri links this to refusing a full gaze at worldly adornment.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r1.anchor: فعيني إذا استحسنت غيركم . . . أمرت الدموع بتأديبها

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r2.claim: In restraint from worldly beauty, the addressee stood on one foot until told to tread the earth with both feet, an image of extreme ascetic effort.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r2.anchor: وقف على وجه الأرض بفرد قدم تصاونا عنها حتى قيل له ( طه )

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r3.claim: Worldly adornment is a trial when it distracts from God, captures the heart, emboldens disobedience, or makes enjoyment lead to arrogance and excess.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r3.anchor: الفتنة ما يشغل به عن الحق ، ويستولي حبه على القلب

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r4.claim: A little lawful provision accompanied by God's pleasure is better than much unlawful worldly wealth accompanied by His displeasure.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r4.anchor: القليل من الحلال - وفيه رضاء الرحمن - خير من الكثير

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r5.claim: Another gloss says a little that keeps one witnessing the Lord is better than much that makes one forget Him.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r5.anchor: ويقال قليل يشهدك ربك خير من كثير ينسيك ربك

BURHAN:v1p415/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p415/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p415/r3.claim: His rule is that words carrying a noun's sense do not take open tā; he lists زهرة, صبغة, زلزلة, تحلة, رحلة, and حمالة.
BURHAN:v1p415/r3.anchor: والضابط لذلك أن ما كان بمعنى الاسم لم تمد تاؤه مثل

BURHAN:v1p3/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p3/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p3/r1.claim: Zarkashi praises the Qur'an's inimitable concision, eloquence and wisdom, its ordered blend of literal and figurative speech, and its varied rhetorical forms and shifts of tone.
BURHAN:v1p3/r1.anchor: وتظافر إيجازه وإعجازه ، وتظافرت حقيقته ومجازه ، وتقارن في الحسن مطالعه ومقاطعه

BURHAN:v1p281/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p281/r1.speaker: أبو شامة
BURHAN:v1p281/r1.claim: Abu Shama interprets the provision of the Lord as the Qur'an.
BURHAN:v1p281/r1.anchor: أبو شامة فى المرشد الوجيز فى قوله تعالى ﴿ ورزق ربك خير وأبقى ﴾ قال يعنى القرآن

BURHAN:v1p281/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p281/r2.speaker: السخاوى
BURHAN:v1p281/r2.claim: Al-Sakhawi says the Qur'an granted to the Prophet is better than the worldly provision given to others.
BURHAN:v1p281/r2.anchor: وقال السخاوى يعنى ما رزقك الله من القرآن خير مما رزقهم من الدنيا

ITQAN:v1p145/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p145/r7.speaker: أبو شامة وغيره
ITQAN:v1p145/r7.claim: Abu Shama and others interpret the Lord's better and more lasting provision as the Qur'an.
ITQAN:v1p145/r7.anchor: وذكر أبو شامة وغيره في قوله تعالى ﴿ ورزق ربك خير وأبقى ﴾ أنه القرآن

SULAMI:v1p453#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r1.claim: The prohibition on admiring worldly life consoles the poor; the next command turns them toward worship and perseverance in prayer.
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه في هذه الآية : تسلية للفقراء وتعزية لهم حيث منع الخلق عن النظر إلى الدنيا على وجه الإستحسان فقال :

SULAMI:v1p453#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r2.speaker: النبي
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r2.claim: A report says the Prophet recited this verse and said that one not consoled by God's consolation will be torn apart by longing for the world; no grading is stated.
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r2.anchor: روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال حين قرأ هذه الآية قال : ' من لم يتعزى بعزاء الله تقطعت نفسه على الدنيا حسرات '

SULAMI:v1p453#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r3.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r3.claim: Avoid whatever feeds satanic whispering, disobedience, egoistic hopes, or attachment to natural habits, since each cuts one off from God.
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r3.anchor: وقال سهل : لا تنظر إلى ما يورثك وسوسة الشيطان ، ومخالفة الرحمن ، وأماني النفس ،

SULAMI:v1p453#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r4.claim: The Lord's provision means contentment with what one owns and renunciation of what one does not own.
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r4.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر في هذه الآية : هو القناعة بما يملكه ، والزهد فيما لا يملكه .

SULAMI:v1p453#4/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r5.claim: Trusting God and being content with Him are the best provisions.
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : من رزق الثقة بالله ، والرضاء عن الله فقد أعطى أفضل الأرزاق .

SULAMI:v1p453#4/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r6.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r6.claim: The Lord's provision is reliance, better and more lasting than seeking and toil.
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان في قوله ﴿ ورزق ربك خير وأبقى ﴾ قال : هو توكل لأنه أبقى للمرء من الطلب ،

ITQAN:v1p49/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p49/r8.speaker: أبو رافع
ITQAN:v1p49/r8.claim: Al-Suyuti argues for another Medinan exception in Ta-Ha: Abu Rafiʿ reports that a Jewish lender demanded collateral for a loan of flour, after which the Prophet said he was trustworthy in heaven and earth and the verse forbidding coveting worldly provision was revealed.
ITQAN:v1p49/r8.anchor: أخرج البزار وأبو يعلى عن أبي رافع قال أضاف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيفا فأرسلني إلى رجل من اليهود

TUSTARI:20:131/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:20:131/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:20:131/r1.claim: Do not look toward worldly delights that bring Satan's whispering, disobedience, the soul's hopes, or ease in familiar habits; each cuts one off from remembering God.
TUSTARI:20:131/r1.anchor: أي لا تنظر إلى ما يورثك وسوسة الشيطان، ومخالفة الرحمن، وأماني النفس

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p147/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p147/r3.speaker: أبو رافع
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p147/r3.claim: Abu Rafi reports that the Prophet sent him to a Jewish man to borrow flour until Rajab; when collateral was demanded, the Prophet affirmed his trustworthiness in heaven and earth, and this verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p147/r3.anchor: عن أبي رافع قال أضاف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيفا فأرسلني إلى رجل من اليهود أن أسلفني دقيقا

DAMGHANI:v1p202/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p202/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p202/r8.claim: Rizq can mean Paradise and its delights.
DAMGHANI:v1p202/r8.anchor: الرزق بمعنى الجنة قوله تعالى في سورة طه

DAMGHANI:v1p220/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p220/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p220/r10.claim: Zīnah can mean the bloom or flower of worldly life; 18:46 and 28:60 are grouped with this gloss.
DAMGHANI:v1p220/r10.anchor: الزينة الزهرة قوله تعالى في سورة يونس

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p324/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p324/r9.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p324/r9.claim: Muqātil interprets the Lord’s better and more lasting provision as Paradise.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p324/r9.anchor: والثامن : الجنة . ومنه قوله تعالى في طه :

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#8/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#8/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#8/r1.claim: Zahrah means the adornment or beauty of worldly life, like the beauty of a plant in bloom.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#8/r1.anchor: و {زهرة الحياة} أي زينتها، وهو من زهرة النبات وحسنه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#8/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#8/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#8/r2.claim: Li-naftinahum means so that We may test them.

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r1.claim: أزواجا may be the direct object of متعنا.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنه منصوب على المفعول به وهو واضح.

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r2.claim: Alternatively, أزواجا is a circumstantial accusative referring to the pronoun in به.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه منصوب على الحال من الهاء في " به ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r3.claim: The construction observes ما once in its form and once in its meaning, which accounts for the plural أزواجا.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r3.anchor: راعى لفظ " ما " مرة، ومعناها أخرى، فلذلك جمع.

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the verb acts on منهم, paraphrasing the object as kinds and people among them.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " ويكون الفعل واقعا على " منهم ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r5.claim: زهرة can be a second object because متعنا is construed with the sense of أعطينا, making أزواجا the first object.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r5.anchor: أحدها: أنه مفعول ثان لأنه ضمن متعنا معنى أعطينا.

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r6.claim: زهرة may be an appositive to أزواجا, either with a deleted إضافة or by treating the people as the very flower.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r6.anchor: الثاني: أن يكون بدلا من " أزواجا " ، وذلك: إما على حذف مضاف

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r7.claim: زهرة may be accusative after an implicit verb indicated by متعنا, understood as جعلنا لهم زهرة.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r7.anchor: الثالث: أن يكون منصوبا بفعل مضمر دل عليه " متعنا " تقديره: جعلنا لهم زهرة.

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats زهرة as an accusative of censure, which he calls نصب على الاختصاص.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r8.anchor: الثالث: نصبه على الذم، قال الزمخشري: " وهو النصب على الاختصاص ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r9.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r9.claim: Some take زهرة as an appositive to the relative pronoun's syntactic position.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r9.anchor: الرابع: أن يكون بدلا من موضع الموصول. قال أبو البقاء: " واختاره بعضهم.

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r10.speaker: آخرون
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r10.claim: Others disallow that apposition because لنفتنهم belongs to the relative clause and would separate it from متعنا.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r10.anchor: وقال آخرون: لا يجوز لأن قوله { لنفتنهم } من صلة " متعنا "

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r11.claim: The author calls the objection to apposition from the relative pronoun's position a sound one.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r11.anchor: بين الصلة والموصول بالأجنبي ". وهو اعتراض حسن.

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r12.claim: Another analysis makes زهرة an appositive to the syntactic position of به.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r12.anchor: الخامس: أن ينتصب على البدل من محل " به ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r13.claim: زهرة may be a circumstantial accusative from the relative ما.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r13.anchor: السادس: أن ينتصب على الحال من " ما " الموصولة.

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r14.claim: It may instead be circumstantial from the pronoun in به; make زهرة indefinite by restoring tanwīn, elided at the meeting of two sukūns, as in the cited line.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r14.anchor: السابع: أنه حال من الهاء في " به " وهو ضمير الموصول فهو كالذي قبله

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r15.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r15.claim: On the circumstantial analysis with an indefinite زهرة, الحياة is construed as an appositive to the relative ما.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r15.anchor: وعلى هذا: فيم جرت الحياة؟ فقيل: على البدل من " ما " الموصولة.

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r16.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r16.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r16.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows زهرة as a specification of ما or of the pronoun in به; the objection that specification cannot be definite is not binding on Kufan principles.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r16.anchor: الثامن: أنه تمييز ل " ما " أو للهاء في " به " قاله الفراء.

SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r17.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r17.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r17.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ disallows making زهرة an adjective of أزواجا because the described noun is indefinite while the adjective is definite; the author answers with the same tanwīn-elision analysis used for the circumstantial reading.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131/r17.anchor: وقد منع أبو البقاء من هذا الوجه بكون الموصوف نكرة، والوصف معرفة،

SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r1.claim: The general reading has a quiescent hāʾ in زهرة; al-Ḥasan, Abū al-Barhasam, and Abū Ḥaywa read it with a fatḥa, likened to two forms of جهرة.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r1.anchor: والعامة على تسكين الهاء. وقرأ الحسن وأبو البرهسم وأبو حيوة بفتحها،

SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari permits زهرة as a plural of زاهر, by analogy with فاجر/فجرة and بار/بررة.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r2.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري أن يكون جمع زاهر كفاجر وفجرة وبار وبررة،

SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r3.speaker: الأصمعي
SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r3.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī reports from Nāfiʿ لنفتنهم with a ḍamma on the initial nūn, from أفتنه meaning to bring him into trial.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r3.anchor: وروى الأصمعي عن نافع " لنفتنهم " بضم النون من أفتنه إذا أوقعه في الفتنة.

SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r4.claim: زهرة, with either a fatḥa or sukūn on hāʾ, means what is pleasing in a flower; the related descriptions زاهر, أزهر, زهراء, and الزهر refer to brightness and radiance.
SAMIN-DURR:20:131#2/r4.anchor: والزهرة: بفتح الهاء وسكونها كنهر ونهر، ما يروق من النور.

ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r1.claim: Azwājan here means men from among them.

ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r2.claim: Zahrah is given with either fatḥa or sukūn on the hāʾ.
ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r2.anchor: و (زهرة) جميعا - بفتح الهاء وتسكينها - و (زهرة)

ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r3.claim: Zahrata is accusative as the object or result of mattaʿnā, meaning God made worldly life a bloom for them.
ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r3.anchor: و (زهرة) منصوب بمعنى متعنا لأن معناه جعلنا لهم

ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r4.claim: The purpose is to make that worldly provision a trial for them.
ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r4.anchor: لنفتنهم فيه). أي لنجعل ذلك فتنة لهم

ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n115/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n115/r1.speaker: most of the commentators
ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n115/r1.claim: Most commentators take azwajan minhum to refer to the deniers of truth discussed in the preceding passages.
ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n115/r1.anchor: According to most of the commentators, this relates to the deniers of the truth spoken of in the preceding passages

ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n115/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n115/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n115/r2.claim: Asad broadens the phrase to mean “so many others,” reading the injunction as a general condemnation of envy rather than one limited to truth-deniers.
ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n115/r2.anchor: since the above injunction has obviously a wider purport, condemning envy in general, I have rendered this expression as "so many others"

ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n116/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n116/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n116/r1.claim: Asad says what God grants a person reflects divine wisdom and is appropriate to that person's decreed destiny.
ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n116/r1.anchor: whatever God grants a person is an outcome of divine wisdom and, therefore, truly appropriate to the destiny which God has decreed for that person

ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n116/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n116/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n116/r2.claim: Alternatively, Asad says the phrase may refer to the hereafter and the spiritual sustenance God gives the righteous.
ASAD-NOTES:20:131#n116/r2.anchor: Alternatively, the phrase may be understood as referring to the life to come and the spiritual sustenance which God bestows upon the righteous.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r1.claim: Across Quranic usage, baqā opposes perishing and denotes enduring good and what lasts with God, including the lasting provision promised in 20:131.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p419/r1.anchor: القرآن نقيض النفاد والفناء، فيما يبقى عند الله من عمل صالح، وما عند الله خير وأبقى

NASHR:v2p322/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p322/r3.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p322/r3.claim: Yaqub reads زهرة with fatḥa on hāʾ; the others use sukūn.
NASHR:v2p322/r3.anchor: فقرأ يعقوب بفتح الهاء وقرأ الباقون بإسكانها

NASHR:v2p80/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p80/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p80/r1.claim: For the imāla in the preceding discussion, the author says the reliably transmitted choice for al-Azraq from Warsh and the other cited reader is fatḥ.
NASHR:v2p80/r1.anchor: والحكم في وجه الإمالة للأزرق عن ورش كذلك والصحيح المأخوذ به عنهما هو الفتح

NASHR:v2p80/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p80/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p80/r5.claim: Imāla at verse endings across eleven sūras depends on six regional counting systems; the Madinan counts guide Nāfiʿ’s readers and the Basran count guides Abū ʿAmr.
NASHR:v2p80/r5.anchor: رءوس الآي الممالة في الإحدى عشر سورة متفق عليها ومختلف فيها

NASHR:v2p80/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p80/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p80/r6.claim: Of five disputed verse endings in Ṭā Hā, the Madinan, Meccan, and Basran counters include both مني هدى and زهرة الحياة الدنيا.
NASHR:v2p80/r6.anchor: وهي قوله في طه مني هدى، زهرة الحياة الدنيا عدهما المدنيان، والمكي، والبصري

QIRAAT-ER:20:131:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:131:11#1/r1.speaker: skn
QIRAAT-ER:20:131:11#1/r1.claim: Fatḥa rather than sukūn on hāʾ changes syllable weight in zahara versus zahra without affecting the root meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:20:131:11#1/r1.anchor: Fatḥa on hāʾ instead of sukūn — zaharata vs. zahrata; morphological variant affecting syllable weight

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r1.claim: The majority read زهرة with a sukūn on the hāʾ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r2.speaker: الحسن وأبو البر هيثم وأبو حيوة وطلحة وحميد وسلام ويعقوب وسهل وعيسى والزهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Abū al-Barr Haytham, Abū Ḥaywa, Ṭalḥa, Ḥumayd, Sallām, Yaʿqūb, Sahl, ʿĪsā, and al-Zuhrī read زهرة with fatḥ on the hāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو البر هيثم وأبو حيوة وطلحة وحميد وسلام ويعقوب وسهل وعيسى والزهري بفتحها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r3.speaker: الأصمعي عن نافع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r3.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī transmits from Nāfiʿ a form with ḍamm on the nūn, from أفتنه, making the person the recipient of the trial.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r3.anchor: وقرأ الأصمعي عن نافع لنفتنهم بضم النون من أفتنه إذا جعل الفتنة واقعة فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r4.claim: The forms زهرة and زهرة are synonymous, just as جهرة and جهرة are synonymous.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r4.anchor: والزهرة والزهرة بمعنى واحد كالجهرة والجهرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows the open-hāʾ form to be a plural of زاهر, describing the worldly people as radiant and attractive in color, faces, and dress.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r5.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري في زهرة المفتوح الهاء أن يكون جمع زاهر نحو كافر وكفرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī contrasts the worldly people's bright complexions and finery with the pallor and austere clothing of believers and the devout.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r6.anchor: وتهلل وجوههم وبهاء زيهم وشارتهم بخلاف ما عليه المؤمنون والصلحاء من شحوب الألوان والتقشف في الثياب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r7.claim: God gives them worldly abundance to test them until their ingratitude makes them deserve punishment, or to punish them for it in the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r7.anchor: ومعنى لنفتنهم فيه أي لنبلوهم حتى يستوجبوا العذاب لوجود الكفران منهم أو لنعذبهم في الآخرة بسببه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r8.claim: The provision God has stored for believers in the afterlife is better than what the worldly people enjoy and lasts longer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r8.anchor: أي ما ذخر لهم من المواهب في الآخرة خير مما متع به هؤلاء في الدنيا وأبقى أي أدوم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r9.claim: One view says even a small, wholesome and lawful provision is better than the abundant but tainted or forbidden provision of the others.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r9.anchor: وقيل: ما رزقهم وإن كان قليلا خير مما رزقوا وإن كان كثير الحلية ذلك وحرميّة هذا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r10.claim: Another view identifies God's provision as prophethood and Islam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r10.anchor: وقيل: ما رزقت من النبوة والإسلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r11.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r11.claim: Another view means the lands and spoils God will open to believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r11.anchor: وقيل: ما يفتح الله على المؤمنين من البلاد والغنائم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r12.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r12.claim: Another view interprets God's provision as contentment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r13.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r13.claim: Another view means God's reward for patience and indifference to worldly abundance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r13.anchor: وقيل: ثواب الله على الصبر وقلة المبالاة بالدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r1.claim: Do not prolong your gaze toward worldly adornments with desire, inclination, or longing.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r1.anchor: أي لاتطل نظرهما بطريق الرغبة والميل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r2.claim: The worldly adornments include children, wealth, homes, clothing, and food.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r2.anchor: من زخارف الدنيا كالبنين والأموال والمنازل والملابس والمطاعم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r3.claim: Azwājan means groups or kinds of disbelievers and is the object of متعنا; the prepositional phrase is fronted for emphasis, and min is explanatory.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r3.anchor: أي أصنافا من الكفرة وهو مفعول متعنا قدم عليه الجار والمجرور للاعتناء به ومن بيانيه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, min is circumstantial and partitive, or describes an omitted object: kinds of worldly enjoyment given to some of them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r4.anchor: وجوز أن يكون حالا من ضمير به ومن تبعيضية مفعول متعنا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r5.claim: Some take the address to the Prophet as intending his community, since he was least attached to worldly adornment and warned against being deceived by it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب له عليه الصلاة والسلام والمراد أمته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r6.claim: The wording permits an ordinary glance; the actual prohibition targets admiration, desire, and inclination, expressed through ellipsis or figurative attribution.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r6.anchor: والكلام على حذف مضاف أو فيه تجوز في النسبة وفي العدول عن لا تنظر إلى ما متعنا به

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r7.claim: Some ascetics avoided even viewing rulers' buildings, fine clothes, and mounts, since the display was intended to impress spectators and looking fulfilled that purpose.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r7.anchor: حتى أنهم لم ينظروا إلى أبنية الظلمة وعدد المسقة في اللباس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r8.claim: Zahrah means the world's adornment and brightness.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r8.anchor: أي زينتها وبهجتها وهو منصوب بمحذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r9.claim: Possible parses include an omitted predicate of جعلنا, a second object through the sense of أعطينا, or a badal from the محل of به; Ibn al-Ḥājib rejects the badal as weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r9.anchor: أي جعلنا لهم زهرة أو بمتعنا على أنه مفعول ثان له لتضمينه معنى أعطينا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r10.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r10.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib objects that an accusative badal from a prepositional phrase is weak and that substituting from a pronoun is disputed.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r10.anchor: وضعفه ابن الحاجب في أماليه لأن إبدال منصوب من محل جار ومجرور ضعيف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r11.claim: Other parses make zahrah a badal from ما with an intervening clause, a badal from azwājan with an implied أصحاب, or a badal that identifies the groups as enjoyment; the last is rejected.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r11.anchor: ومثل ذلك ما قيل إنه بدل من ما الموصولة لما فيه من الفصل بالبدل بين الصلة ومعمولها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r12.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r12.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reportedly treats zahrah as an adjective of azwājan, but al-Alusi rejects the definiteness mismatch in a descriptive accusative.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r12.anchor: وحكى عن الفراء أوصفه أزواجا ورد ذلك لتعريف التمييز وتعريف وصف النكرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r13.claim: Further suggestions are a specification of ما or its pronoun, a circumstantial accusative, a badal from ما with الحياة genitive, or an accusative of censure; al-Alusi discusses objections to each.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r13.anchor: على أنه تمييز لما أو لضمير به وحكى عن الفراء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r14.claim: The proposed censure reading is resisted because the verse acknowledges natural attraction; al-Alusi replies that calling it a bloom of worldly life itself censures it as a base desire lacking guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283#2/r14.anchor: بأن المقام يأباه لأن المراد أن النفوس مجبولة على النظر إليها والرغبة فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows zahrah as the plural of زاهر, an adjective for disbelievers radiant in worldly life, with a circumstantial parse.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r1.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري كون زهرة بالتحريك جمع زاهر ككافر وكفرة وهو وصف لأزواجا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r2.claim: Al-Alusi says the adjective ordinarily denotes a stable quality, not a temporary state, so its إضافة would not be verbal; the circumstantial interpretation is also poor.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r2.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن المتبادر من هذه الصفة قصد الثبوت لا الحدوث فلا تكون إضافتها لفظية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r3.claim: The phrase attaches to متعنا: God gives them worldly enjoyment as a test, or to punish them for it in the afterlife, warning of a bad end after present beauty.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r3.anchor: متعلق بمتعنا أي لنعاملهم معاملة من يبتليهم ويختبرهم فيه أو لنعذبهم في الآخرة بسببه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r4.speaker: الأصمعي عن عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r4.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī reports from ʿĀṣim the reading لنفتنهم with ḍamma on the nūn, from أفتنه, meaning to make the trial occur in it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r4.anchor: وقرأ الأصمعي عن عاصم لنفتنهم بضم النون من أفتنه إذا جعل الفتنة واقعة فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r5.claim: The Prophet's provision may mean what is stored for the afterlife, worldly prophethood and guidance, promised conquest and spoils, or contentment.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r5.anchor: أي ما ادخر لك في الآخرة أو رزقك في الدنيا من النبوة والهدى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r6.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r6.claim: The worldly provision of prophethood and guidance best suits this context, according to Ṣāḥib al-Kashf.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r6.anchor: وادعى صاحب الكشف أنه أنسب بهذا المقام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r7.claim: The provision is better because it is among the noblest things people seek and is safe from ruin; it lasts itself or in its effects, unlike worldly enjoyment.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r7.anchor: لأنه مع كونه في نفسه من أجل ما يتنافس فيه المتنافسون مأمون الغائلة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r8.speaker: الحسن وأبو حيوة وطلحة وحميد وسلام ويعقوب وسهل وعيسى والزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Abū Ḥaywah, Ṭalḥah, Ḥumayd, Salām, Yaʿqūb, Sahl, ʿĪsā, and al-Zuhrī read zahrah with fatḥa on the hāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وابو حيوة وطلحة وحميد وسلام ويعقوب وسهل وعيسى والزهري زهرة بفتح الهاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r9.speaker: ابن جني
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r9.claim: Ibn Jinnī reports that Basran grammarians treat a glottal letter after a fatḥa as moving only in dialectal forms; Kūfans generalize movement unless blocked.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r9.anchor: وفي المحتسب لابن جنى مذهب اصحابنا في كل حرف حلق ساكن بعد فتحة أنه لا يحرك إلا على أنه لغة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r10.speaker: الكوفيين
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r10.claim: Al-Kūfiyyūn generalize movement of the second consonant when it is pharyngeal, even without a cited dialect, unless an impediment prevents it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284/r10.anchor: ومذهب الكوفيين أنه يطرد تحريك الثاني لكونه حرفا حلقيا وان لم يسمع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r1.speaker: علي وابن عباس وقتادة وأكثر الصحابة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r1.claim: Most authorities say the Fatiha is Meccan, among the earliest revelations; this is reported from Ali, Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and most Companions.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r1.anchor: وهو المروى عن علي وإبن عباس وقتادة وأكثر الصحابة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r2.speaker: مجاهد
