ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r2.claim: Mujahid says the Fatiha is Medinan; he is said to have been alone in this view, which was counted as a mistake.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r2.anchor: وعن مجاهد أنها مدنية وقد تفرد بذلك حتى عد هفوة منه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r3.claim: Another view says it descended in Mecca when prayer became obligatory and again in Medina when the qibla changed, affirming its continued place in prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r3.anchor: وقيل نزلت بمكة حين فرضت الصلاة وبالمدينة لما حولت القبلة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r4.claim: A further view that some of the Fatiha is Meccan and some Medinan is weak, in Al-Alusi’s judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r4.anchor: وقيل بعضها مكي وبعضها مدني ولا يخفى ضعفه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r5.claim: The Meccan case appeals to 15:87, which scholars and Ibn Abbas identify as referring to the seven oft-repeated verses; however, Ibn Abbas and others also interpret these as the seven long surahs.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r5.anchor: على مكيتها بآية الحجر ( ولقد آتيناك سبعا من المثاني والقرآن العظيم ) وهي مكية لنص العلماء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r6.claim: Al-Alusi prefers Companion testimony from eyewitnesses to revelation as the strongest evidence, since the Meccan argument depends on interpreting the seven oft-repeated verses as the Fatiha.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r6.anchor: والأقوى الإستدلال بالنقل عن الصحابة الذين شاهدوا الوحي التنزيل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r7.claim: The objection that God cannot promise a gift before its delivery is weakened by Quranic past tense used for a future certainty, as in 48:1, although the emphatic wording and the link to 20:131 suggest prior occurrence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r7.anchor: وهذا وإن كان خلاف الظاهر لا سيما مع إيراد اللام وكلمة ( قد ) ووروده في معرض المنة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r8.claim: Al-Alusi rejects repeated descent: revelation is a manifestation from the unseen to the visible and cannot recur; claims of different benefits, readings, or presence of the basmala do not prove a second descent, and reports merely establish occurrence rather than cause it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r8.anchor: والظهور بها لا يقبل التكرر فإن ظهور الظاهر ظاهر البطلان كتحصيل الحاصل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r9.claim: Surah may derive from sur, a remnant, or from the enclosing wall of a building; it may also derive from elevation, as in al-Nabigha’s line where sura means rank or eminence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r9.anchor: ألم تر أن الله أعطاك سورة ترى كل ملك حولها يتذبذب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r10.claim: A surah is an independent Quranic unit with an opening and conclusion; the alternative definition as a self-contained section would require Ayat al-Kursi’s surah status to be established by transmitted designation. Surah names are established by reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r10.anchor: وحدها قرآن يشتمل على ذي فاتحة وخاتمة وقيل طائفة مستقلة لتخرج آية الكرسي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r11.claim: Al-Alusi dismisses the prohibition on saying Sura X: Anas’s report is weak or fabricated, while Ibn Umar’s is authentic in chain but only his own statement.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r11.anchor: إذ حديث أنس ضعيف أو موضوع وحديث ابن عمر موقوف عليه وإن روى عنه بسند صحيح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r12.claim: Fatiha is grammatically a descriptive noun for the first part that opens the whole; it may be a transferred adjective or a verbal noun used for its object, while instrumental and causal derivations are less apt and a relational derivation is possible but weaker.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r12.anchor: والفاتحة ) في الأصل صفة جعلت إما لأول الشيء لكونه واسطة في فتح الكل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r13.claim: Al-Alusi says the Kitab is the concrete whole, so Fatiha is first relative to this particular compilation, which exists in divine knowledge, the Preserved Tablet, or Bayt al-Izza; the first genitive is name-to-named and the second means of, not from.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p33/r13.anchor: والكتاب ( هو المجموع الشخصي وفتح الفاتحة بالقياس إليه لا إلى القدر المشترك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r1.speaker: أبو رافع
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r1.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ reports that a guest came to the Prophet, who sent him to a Jewish man for flour on credit until Rajab; the man required collateral, so the Prophet sent his iron armor, and the verse was revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو رافع: نزل برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r2.claim: The command means not to look at what God has granted them for worldly enjoyment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r2.anchor: لا تنظر، {إلى ما متعنا به} أعطينا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r3.claim: Azwājan here means kinds or classes among them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r4.claim: The “flower” of worldly life means its adornment and splendor.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r4.anchor: أي زينتها وبهجتها، وقرأ يعقوب زهرة بفتح الهاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r5.speaker: يعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r5.claim: Yaʿqūb reads zahrah with fatḥa on the hāʾ; the general reading has sukūn.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب زهرة بفتح الهاء وقرأ العامة بجزمها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r6.claim: God makes their abundance a trial: He increases their blessing, and they respond with greater disbelief and transgression.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r6.anchor: بأن أزيد لهم النعمة فيزيدوا كفرا وطغيانا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r7.claim: The Lord’s provision refers to Paradise in the hereafter.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r8.speaker: أبي بن كعب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r8.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says that reliance on God prevents regret, fixation on others’ possessions prolongs grief, and measuring blessing by food, drink, and clothing leaves one with little work and imminent punishment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303#2/r8.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب: من لم يتعز بعز الله تقطعت نفسه حسرات

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r1.claim: Do not gaze at others' possessions with admiration or wish to possess them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r1.anchor: { ولا تمدن عينيك } أي نظر عينيك

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r2.claim: The phrase means categories of unbelievers; it may also describe the pronoun in به, with منهم as the object and the possessions understood as belonging to some groups or people.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r3.claim: زهرة الحياة الدنيا may be governed by an elided verb indicated by متعنا or به, apposed to the object or أزواجا with an implied noun, or used as a rebuke; it means worldly adornment and splendor.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r3.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف دل عليه { متعنا } أو { به } على تضمينه معنى أعطينا

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r4.speaker: يعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r4.claim: Yaʿqūb reads the word with fatḥa, either a dialect form or a collective meaning worldly flourish, depicting their finery in contrast with believers' asceticism.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r4.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب بالفتح وهو لغة كالجهرة في الجهرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r5.claim: The worldly gifts may be a trial or a means of punishment in the afterlife.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r6.claim: The Lord's provision may be what He has stored for the addressee in the afterlife, or the guidance and prophethood He has granted.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:131/r6.anchor: وما ادخر لك في الآخرة، أو ما رزقك من الهدى والنبوة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r1.claim: The Lord's provision is better than what unbelievers receive in this world and does not end.

DURR-FULL:v5p612/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r1.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports the Prophet’s fear that worldly bloom would be opened to the community; the Prophet defines it as the earth’s blessings.
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن ما أخوف ما أخاف عليكم

DURR-FULL:v5p612/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses the flower of worldly life as its adornment.
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {زهرة الحياة الدنيا} قال: زينة الحياة الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v5p612/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r3.claim: Qatāda explains the worldly gifts as a test for their recipients.
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {زهرة الحياة الدنيا} قال: زينة الحياة الدنيا {لنفتنهم فيه} قال: لنبتليهم فيه

DURR-FULL:v5p612/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r4.claim: Qatāda says the Lord’s provision is better and more lasting than the worldly bloom granted to others.
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {زهرة الحياة الدنيا} قال: زينة الحياة الدنيا {لنفتنهم فيه} قال: لنبتليهم فيه {ورزق ربك خير وأبقى} قال: مما متع به هؤلاء من زهرة الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v5p612/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r5.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r5.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the Lord’s provision as the provision of Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r5.anchor: عن السدي في قوله: {ورزق ربك خير وأبقى} يقول: رزق الجنة

DURR-FULL:v5p612/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r6.speaker: زياد الصدعي
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r6.claim: Ziyād al-Ṣudāʿī reports the Prophet saying that God guarantees provision for whoever seeks knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r6.anchor: عن زياد الصدعي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: من طلب العلم تكفل الله برزقه

DURR-FULL:v5p612/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r7.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports that angels shade and bless the livelihood of one who sets out to seek knowledge, without reducing or withholding their provision.
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r7.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: من غدا في طلب العلم أظلت عليه الملائكة وبورك له في معيشته ولم ينقص من رزقه

DURR-FULL:v5p612/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r10.speaker: عروة
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r10.claim: ʿUrwa would recite the warning against coveting worldly goods after visiting the rich, then urge his household to keep up prayer.
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r10.anchor: عن عروة أنه كان إذا دخل على أهل الدنيا فرأى من دنياهم طرفا فإذا رجع إلى أهله فدخل الدار قرأ {ولا تمدن عينيك} إلى قوله: {نحن نرزقك} ثم يقول: الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v5p613/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r4.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r4.claim: ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr advised anyone dazzled by worldly adornment to return to their family, command prayer, and persevere, citing the verse’s warning against coveting such goods.
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r4.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة قال: قال لنا أبي: إذا رأى أحدكم شيئا من زينة الدنيا وزهرتها فليأت أهله وليأمر أهله بالصلاة وليصطبر عليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r1.claim: After commanding patience with what they say, God forbids marveling at the disbelievers’ wealth and children; their worldly provision serves divine purposes, including establishing proof against them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r1.anchor: أعقب أمره بالصبر على ما يقولونه بنهيه عن الإعجاب بما ينعم به من تنعم من المشركين بأموال وبنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r2.claim: Azwāj here evokes families and households: the provision enjoyed by people and their spouses includes each partner’s beauty and shared goods such as children, furnishings, and homes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r2.anchor: وذكر الأزواج هنا لدلالته على العائلات والبيوت ، أي إلى ما متعناهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r3.claim: Extending the eyes means looking for a long time in amazement, not admiration, like extending a hand toward something desired.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r3.anchor: ومد العينين : مستعمل في إطالة النظر للتعجيب لا للإعجاب ، شبه ذلك بمد اليد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r4.claim: Zahrah, with fatḥa on zāʾ and a still hāʾ, is a flower or plant blossom; figuratively it is the dazzling adornment of worldly life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r4.anchor: والزهرة بفتح الزاي وسكون الهاء : واحدة الزهر ، وهو نور الشجر والنباتت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r5.claim: Worldly adornment includes clothing, livestock, gardens, women, and children, as in the verse about worldly enjoyment and its adornment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r5.anchor: فزهرة الحياة : زينة الحياة ، أي زينة أمور الحياة من اللباس والأنعام والجنان والنساء والبنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r6.claim: Zahrata al-ḥayāh al-dunyā is an accusative circumstantial phrase describing the relative pronoun in mā.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r6.anchor: على الحال من اسم الموصول في قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r7.claim: Most readers pronounce zahrah with a still hāʾ; Yaʿqūb reads the hāʾ with fatḥa, a dialectal form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور زهرة بسكون الهاء . وقرأه يعقوب بفتح الهاء وهي لغة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r8.claim: Li-naftinahum attaches to mattaʿnā, and fī expresses figurative containment: each kind of provision carries a fitting trial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r8.anchor: لنفتنهم } متعلق ب { متعنا } . و ( في ) للظرفية المجازية ، أي ليحصل فتنتهم في خلاله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r9.claim: The lām marks figurative consequence rather than actual motive, as in Pharaoh’s household taking Moses in so he would become their enemy and grief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r9.anchor: واللام للعلة المجازية التي هي عاقبة الشيء ، مثل قوله تعالى : { فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r10.claim: Many interrelated features of social organization lead God to grant worldly adornment; its actual outcome is a trial in their faith, treated as though it were the motive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p339#2/r10.anchor: وإنما متعهم الله بزهرة الدنيا لأسباب كثيرة متسلسلة عن نظم الاجتماع فكانت لهم فتنة في دينهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r1.claim: Fitnah is disturbance and mental turmoil from fear, anticipation, or confused affairs; shirk brings disbelievers gloom and apprehension, and their afterlife trial is evident.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r1.anchor: والفتنة : اضطراب النفس وتبلبل البال من خوف أو توقع أو التواء الأمور ، وكانوا لا يخلون من ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r2.claim: Fī is used for figurative containment, illustrated by Sabrah ibn ʿAmr al-Faqʿasī’s verse and the command to provide and clothe dependents therein.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r2.anchor: في قول سبرة بن عمرو الفقعسي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r3.claim: The concluding statement explains that believers’ God-given provision is better and more lasting than disbelievers’ attractive but inwardly troubled life, and its benefit endures through gratitude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r3.anchor: إلى آخره يفيد أن ما يبدو للناظر من حسن شارتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r4.claim: The possessive phrase honors the provision: although all sustenance comes from God, disbelievers’ provision is treated as detached because it is mixed with anger and ingratitude’s consequences.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r4.anchor: فإضافة { رزق ربك } إضافة تشريف ، وإلا فإن الرزق كله من الله ، ولكن رزق الكافرين لما خالطه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r5.claim: Khayr is a relative comparison across dimensions: some goods benefit now but harm later, some mix benefits with trials, and some fit strongly or weakly; here it favors safety from harms and trials.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p341/r5.anchor: و { خير } تفضيل ، والخيرية حقيقة اعتبارية تختلف باختلاف نواحيها . فمنها : خير لصاحبه في العاجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r1.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r1.claim: An account says the Prophet, short of food for a guest, sought barley from a Jew who demanded collateral; he pledged his armor, and the verse was said to be revealed then.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r1.anchor: قال بعض الناس سبب هذه الآية أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، نزل به ضيف فلم يكن عنده شيء فبعث إلى يهودي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r2.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r2.claim: Abū Muḥammad rejects this occasion: the sūra is Meccan, while the pledge occurred in Medina late in the Prophet’s life, and he died with the armor pledged in that incident.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r2.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا معترض أن يكون سببا لأن السورة مكية والقصة المذكورة مدنية في آخر عمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r3.claim: The verse continues the prior warning about earlier nations and delayed punishment by telling the Prophet to discount opponents, endure their words, and turn from their wealth, which will lead to disgrace.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r3.anchor: وإنما الظاهر أن الآية متناسقة مع ما قبلها وذلك أن الله تعالى وبخهم على ترك الاعتبار بالأمم السالفة ثم توعدهم بالعذاب المؤجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r4.claim: ‘Do not extend your eyes’ is stronger than ‘do not look’: extending one’s gaze implies covetous desire, while looking need not.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r4.anchor: وقوله ولا تمدن عينيك أبلغ من ولا تنظر، لأن الذي يمد بصره إنما يحمله على ذلك حرص مقترن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r5.claim: Azwāj means kinds or varieties, referring to groups and classes of people given worldly goods.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r5.anchor: و «الأزواج» الأنواع فكأنه قال إلى ما متعنا به أقواما منهم وأصنافا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r6.claim: The worldly favors of the disbelievers are likened to a blossom that soon fades, like their condition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى: زهرة الحياة الدنيا شبه نعم هؤلاء الكفار بالزهر وهو ما اصفر من النور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r7.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r7.claim: One explanation takes zahr as flower in general: it looks attractive but soon vanishes, as do the disbelievers’ circumstances.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r7.anchor: وقيل «الزهر» النور جملة لأن الزهر له منظر ثم يضمحل فكذلك حال هؤلاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r8.claim: Zahrata may be accusative as a circumstantial description, since its definiteness is not complete.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r8.anchor: ونصب زهرة يجوز أن ينصب على الحال وذلك أن تعرفها ليس بمحض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r9.claim: One group reads zahrata with a still hāʾ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r10.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r10.claim: Another group reads zahrata with a fatḥa on the hāʾ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r11.claim: God gives them these goods to test them; their corrupt use turns the gift into a trial for which they will be requited with evil.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r11.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم، أن ذلك إنما هو ليختبرهم به ويجعله فتنة لهم وأمرا يجازون عليه بالسوء لفساد تقلبهم فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r12.claim: God’s provision for the righteous is better and more enduring; the provision of the afterlife surpasses worldly provision.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r12.anchor: ورزق الله تعالى الذي أحله للمتقين من عباده خير وأبقى أي رزق الدنيا خير ورزق الآخرة أبقى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r17.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r17.claim: When Urwa saw reports about rulers, he hurried home, recited this verse through ‘and more lasting,’ then called people to prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r17.anchor: وروي أن عروة بن الزبير رضي الله عنه كان إذا رأى شيئا من أخبار السلاطين وأحوالهم بادر إلى منزله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r1.speaker: أبو رافع مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r1.claim: Abu Rafiʿ reports that after a Jewish seller demanded collateral for flour on credit, the Prophet offered his iron armor; the verse then consoled him about worldly life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r1.anchor: سبب نزولها ما روى أبو رافع مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال نزل ضيف برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فدعاني فأرسلني إلى رجل من اليهود يبيع طعاما فقال قل له إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول بعني كذا وكذا من الدقيق أو اسلفني إلى هلال رجب فأتيته فقلت له ذلك فقال اليهودي والله لا أبيعه ولا أسلفه إلا برهن فأتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأخبرته فقال والله لو باعني أو أسلفني لقضيته وإني لأمين في السماء أمين في الأرض اذهب بدرعي الحديد اليه فنزلت هذه الآية تعزية له عن الدنيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r2.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says that whoever does not console himself with God's consolation will be consumed by grief over worldly life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r2.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب من لم يتعز بعزاء الله تقطعت نفسه حسرات على الدنيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r3.claim: The author says he explained this verse previously at the end of 15:88.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r3.anchor: وقد مضى تفسير هذه الآية في آخر الحجر 88

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن والزهري ويعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud, al-Hasan, al-Zuhri, and Yaʿqub read zahra with fatḥa on the hāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود والحسن والزهري ويعقوب زهرة بفتح الهاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says zahra is accusative by association with mattaʿnā: God made worldly life a splendor for them as a trial.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج وهو منصوب بمعنى متعنا لأن معنى متعنا جعلنا لهم الحياة الدنيا زهرة لنفتنهم فيه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r6.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains “to test them” as “to try them.”

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r7.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r7.claim: The commentators describe worldly life's flower as its beauty, freshness, and pleasing appearance, like a plant's blossom.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r7.anchor: قال المفسرون زهرة الدنيا بهجتها وغضارتها وما يروق الناظر منها عند رؤيته وهو من زهرة النبات وحسنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r8.claim: The “provision of your Lord” is explained either as the reward of the afterlife or as contentment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p335/r8.anchor: فيه قولان أحدهما أنه ثوابه في الآخرة والثاني القناعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r1.claim: The Prophet must not gaze at the affluent and their blessings: they are a fading flower and passing pleasure given as a test, and few servants give thanks.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses “groups among them” as the wealthy; God has given the Prophet better, as also stated in the linked passage about the seven oft-repeated verses and Quran.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r3.claim: The afterlife reward God has stored for His Messenger is immense beyond description; the promise that his Lord will give until he is content confirms that God's provision is better and more lasting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r3.anchor: ما ادخره الله تعالى لرسوله في الدار الآخرة أمر عظيم لا يحد ولا يوصف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r4.claim: In an account in Sahih, Umar saw the Prophet lying on a coarse mat with little in the room and wept at the contrast with Khosrow and Caesar; the Prophet replied that their good things were hastened for them in worldly life.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r4.anchor: وفي الصحيح: أن عمر بن الخطاب لما دخل علي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في تلك المشربة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r5.claim: Despite being able to possess wealth, the Prophet was the most ascetic: he distributed what came to him among God's servants and saved nothing for the next day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r5.anchor: أزهد الناس في الدنيا مع القدرة عليها، إذا حصلت له ينفقها هكذا وهكذا، في عباد الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r6.claim: A report from Abu Sa'id says the Prophet feared most what God might open of worldly bloom; he defined that bloom as the earth's blessings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " إن أخوف ما أخاف عليكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r7.speaker: قتادة والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r7.claim: Qatada and al-Suddi interpret the flower of worldly life as its adornment.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326#2/r8.claim: Qatada glosses the phrase as “so that We may test them in it.”

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r5.speaker: أبوه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r5.claim: Hishām's father would recite these verses after seeing worldly wealth, then urge his own household to pray.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r5.anchor: عن هشام، عن أبيه؛ أنه كان إذا دخل على أهل الدنيا، فرأى من دنياهم طرفا فإذا رجع إلى أهله

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r1.claim: The verse follows the account of the disbelievers and their punishment by showing their worldly state, so believers should not be dazzled by them.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r1.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر الكفار وما أعد لهم، بين حالهم في الدنيا فلا يغتر أحد بهم

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r2.claim: The command means not to look toward worldly goods bestowed on others.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r2.anchor: أي: لا تنظر، قيل: نظر رغبة

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r3.claim: One explanation is that the prohibited gaze is one of desire.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r3.anchor: نظر رغبة، وقيل: نظر تأسف على فائت

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r4.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r4.claim: Another explanation is a regretful gaze at what one has missed.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r4.anchor: نظر تأسف على فائت (إلى ما متعنا به)

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r5.claim: The phrase means what God gave them to enjoy among the pleasures of worldly life.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r5.anchor: أعطيناهم ليتمتعوا بها من نعيم الدنيا

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r6.claim: A reported reading takes azwājan as people among them, rather than as a description of the worldly goods.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r6.anchor: قيل: أزواجا من بعضهم لا من نعت المتاع، ثم اختلفوا

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r7.speaker: بعضهم
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r7.claim: Azwājan means their peers and likenesses, since they resemble one another in turning away from right guidance.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r7.anchor: فقال بعضهم: معناه أمثالا وأشباها؛ لأنهم أشكال في الذهاب عن الصواب

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r8.speaker: بعضهم
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r8.claim: Azwājan can mean males and females.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم: أزواجا أراد الذكر والأنثى

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r9.claim: Azwājan may describe the provisions themselves, meaning varieties of worldly delight.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r9.anchor: وقيل: هو من نعت المتاع أي: أصنافا من نعيم الدنيا

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r10.claim: Azwājan may mean individual members, one after another from a group.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r10.anchor: وقيل: أزواجا آحادا؛ لأن الواحد بعد الواحد من الجماعة، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r11.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r11.claim: Zahrat al-dunyā means its adornment; Qatada and others give this explanation.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r11.anchor: زهرة الحياة الدنيا قيل: زينتها، عن قتادة وغيره

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r12.claim: Worldly life is likened to a flower because it disappears quickly.

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r13.claim: The Prophet describes worldly life as sweet and green, paralleling the image of transient beauty.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r13.anchor: قول النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم -: حلوة خضرة، لنفتنهم فيه

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r14.claim: God tests them with what they receive, treating them as those being tested so that the truthful and grateful are distinguished from the false and ungrateful.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r14.anchor: لنفتنهم فيه أي: لنختبرهم، ومعناه نعاملهم معاملة المختبر فيما أوتوا؛ ليظهر المحق من المبطل

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r15.claim: The test includes the obligations wealth entails, including alms and duties concerning property, livestock, enslaved men, and enslaved women.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r15.anchor: وذلك أنه يلزمه عند إيتاء الزكاة تكاليف على ما يلزمه في الأموال والدواب وفي العبيد والجواري

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r16.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r16.claim: The test is the hardship of commanding wealthy rulers to follow the Prophet and his impoverished believers.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r16.anchor: قيل: أمرهم وهم أغنياء وملوك وكبراء باتباع النبي

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r17.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r17.claim: A further explanation takes the testing as punishment in this life and the next for the blessings they received.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r17.anchor: وقيل: نفتنهم نعذبهم بما أوتوا من ذلك فنعذبهم بعذاب الدنيا والآخرة، عن أبي مسلم.

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r18.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r18.claim: Testing them can mean ordering them to spend, pay alms, perform pilgrimage, and wage jihad.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r18.anchor: وقيل: نفتنهم بأن أمرناهم بإنفاقه والزكوات والحج والجهاد

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r19.claim: Rizq here means a gift or provision from the Lord.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r19.anchor: ورزق ربك أي: عطاء ربك، قيل: الذي وعدك

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r20.claim: The preferred explanation is that God's promised reward in the hereafter is better and more enduring than the worldly enjoyment given to them.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r20.anchor: قيل: الذي وعدك في الآخرة خير وأبقى مما متعنا به هؤلاء في الدنيا، عن أبي علي، وأبي مسلم، وجماعة. وقيل:

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r21.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r21.claim: Another view says what God gave the Prophet in this life with a good final outcome is better, since the others' end is the Fire.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r21.anchor: وقيل: ما أعطاك في الدنيا مع حسن العاقبة خير مما أعطاهم إذ كان عاقبتهم النار، وقيل: ما أعطاك

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r22.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r22.claim: A further view says God's gift is better because it is not coveted as the disbelievers' wealth is coveted.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r22.anchor: وقيل: ما أعطاك ربك خير؛ لأنه لا يغتنم كما تغتنم أموال الكفار، والأول الوجه

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r23.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r23.anchor: وأبقى أدوم وأمر أهلك قيل: أهل بيتك وأهل دينك بالصلاة

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r31.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r31.speaker: هشام بن عروة بن الزبير
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r31.claim: Hisham reports that when Urwa ibn al-Zubayr saw the rulers' possessions, he went home, recited these verses, and called people to prayer.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r31.anchor: وعن هشام بن عروة بن الزبير قال: كان عروة بن الزبير إذا رأى ما عند السلطان دخل بيته

JISHUMI:v7p4774/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4774/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4774/r1.claim: The verse disciplines believers to practice worldly renunciation and contentment with little, avoid being deceived by worldly life, and strengthens the Prophet when he sees disbelievers' blessings.
JISHUMI:v7p4774/r1.anchor: على تأديب من الله تعالى لعباده في الزهد في الدنيا، والقناعة بقليلها

JISHUMI:v7p4774/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4774/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4774/r2.claim: The reward God has prepared in Paradise for believers is better and more enduring, encouraging pursuit of the hereafter.
JISHUMI:v7p4774/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن ما أعد الله للمؤمنين من ثواب الجنة خير وأدوم، وفيه ترغيب في أمر الآخرة.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r1.claim: To stretch one’s eyes is to prolong one’s gaze without turning away, admiring and desiring to possess what is seen.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r1.anchor: مد النظر : تطويله ، وأن لا يكاد يرده ، استحسانا للمنظور إليه وإعجابا به ، وتمنيا أن يكون له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r2.claim: The warning recalls onlookers who wished for Qarun’s wealth at 28:79 and were answered by people of knowledge and faith at 28:80.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r2.anchor: كما فعل نظارة قارون حين قالوا : { الدنيا ياليت لنا مثل ما أوتى قارون إنه لذو حظ عظيم } ( القصص : 79 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r3.claim: An incidental glance followed by lowering the eyes is excused; the verse rebukes sustained looking, a habit encouraged by worldly adornment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r3.anchor: وفيه أن النظر غير الممدود معفو عنه ، وذلك مثل نظر من باده الشيء بالنظر ثم غض الطرف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r4.speaker: العلماء من أهل التقوى
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r4.claim: Pious scholars insist that believers must avert their gaze from the buildings, clothing, mounts, and other display of oppressors and profligates, since looking fulfills their desire for an audience and encourages them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r4.anchor: ولقد شدد العلماء من أهل التقوى في وجوب غض البصر عن أبنية الظلمة وعدد الفسقة في اللباس والمراكب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r5.claim: Azwājan means groups or kinds of disbelievers.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r6.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is circumstantial from the pronoun, with the verb applying to “them”: people among those whom God has given enjoyment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن ينتصب حالا من هاء الضمير ، والفعل واقع على { منهم } كأنه قال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r7.claim: One analysis puts zahrah in the accusative as a term of censure or specification.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r7.anchor: على الذم وهو النصب على الاختصاص

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r8.claim: A second analysis treats muttiʿnā as carrying the sense “gave and bestowed,” making zahrah its second object.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r8.anchor: وعلى تضمين { متعنا } معنى أعطينا وخولنا ، وكونه مفعولا ثانيا له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r9.claim: A third analysis makes zahrah a substitute for the case position of the prepositional phrase.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r9.anchor: وعلى إبداله من محل الجار والمجرور

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r10.claim: A fourth analysis makes zahrah a substitute for azwājan, with an implied “possessors of.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r10.anchor: وعلى إبداله من أزواجا ، على تقدير ذوي زهرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r11.claim: With its vowel moved, zahrah retains its sense of adornment and beauty; the author compares jahrah and cites the reading “Show us God” at 4:153.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r11.anchor: معنى الزهرة بعينه وهو الزينة والبهجة ، كما جاء في الجهرة الجهرة . وقرىء : { أرنا الله } ( النساء : 153 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r12.claim: Alternatively, it may be a plural of zāhir, describing worldly people as radiant in complexion and appearance from their indulgence, unlike the pallor and coarse clothing of the righteous.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r12.anchor: وأن تكون جمع زاهر ، وصفا لهم بأنهم زاهرو هذه الدنيا ، لصفاء ألوانهم مما يلهون ويتنعمون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r13.claim: Their worldly enjoyment may be a test that makes them deserve punishment because they are ungrateful, or it may mean God will punish them in the afterlife for it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r13.anchor: لنبلوهم حتى يستوجبوا العذاب ، لوجود الكفران منهم . أو لنعذبهم في الآخرة بسببه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r14.claim: The Lord’s provision may mean the stored reward of the afterlife, better in itself and more lasting.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r14.anchor: هو ما ادخر له من ثواب الآخرة الذي هو خير منه في نفسه وأدوم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r15.claim: Alternatively, it means the blessing of Islam and prophethood that God grants.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r15.anchor: أو ما رزقه من نعمة الإسلام والنبوة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p97/r16.claim: It may mean lawful provision: the disbelievers’ wealth is often stolen or illicit, and God ascribes only what is lawful and pure to Himself; forbidden wealth is not called provision.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p99/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p99/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p99/r1.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ reports that the Prophet sent him to request a loan from a Jewish man until Rajab; the man demanded collateral, so the Prophet pledged his iron armor and said he was trustworthy in heaven and earth. The source says this verse was revealed in connection with the incident; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p99/r1.anchor: بعثني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى يهودي وقال

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r2.claim: A second interpretation takes extending the eyes as grief or regret.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r3.claim: أزواجا means kinds or categories, from the idea of pairing.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r4.claim: Qatada interprets the world's زهرة as its adornment.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r5.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r5.claim: Ibn Bahr interprets the trial as punishing them through the worldly adornment they were given.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r5.anchor: لنفتنهم أي لنعذبهم به , قاله ابن بحر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r6.claim: Another possible sense is that worldly gifts turn them away from their interests.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r7.claim: One explanation is contentment with what one possesses and renunciation of what one does not possess.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r7.anchor: أنه القناعة بما يملكه والزهد فيما لا يملكه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r8.claim: Another explanation is that God's afterlife reward is better and more lasting than the worldly provision given to others.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r8.anchor: وثواب ربك في الآخرة خير وأبقى مما متعنا به هؤلاء في الدنيا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r9.claim: A further possibility is that lawful provision that remains is better than abundant provision that leads to transgression.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r9.anchor: أن يكون الحلال المبقي خيرا من الكثير المطغي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r10.speaker: أبو رافع
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r10.claim: Abu Rafiʿ reports that the verse was revealed after a Jewish lender demanded collateral for food borrowed by the Prophet, who grieved and offered his armor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r10.anchor: ما رواه أبو رافع أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم استلف من يهودي طعاما فأبى أن يسلفه إلا برهن

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r11.claim: A report says that after this verse was revealed, the Prophet had a caller announce that neglecting God's discipline leaves the soul cut by regret for worldly life.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r11.anchor: وروى أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مناديه فنادى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r1.claim: Extending the gaze means prolonging it and holding it in admiration of what is seen.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r1.anchor: ومد النظر تطويله وأن لا يكاد يرده استحسانا للمنظور إليه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r2.claim: A passing, unextended glance is excused: one may first notice something, then lower the gaze.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r2.anchor: وفيه أن النظر غير الممدود معفو عنه وذلك أن يبادر الشيء بالنظر ثم بغض الطرف

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan warns against admiring the ostentation of profligates and urges seeing the humiliation of disobedience upon them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r3.anchor: حتى قال الحسن لا تنظروا إلى دقدقة هما ليج الفسقة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r4.claim: The ostentatious possessions are displayed to attract onlookers; gazing at them rewards and encourages their owners to keep displaying them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r4.anchor: إنما اتخذوا هذه الاشياء لعيون النظارة فالناظر إليها محصل لعرهم ومغر لهم على اتخاذها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r5.claim: The enjoyment is given to classes among the disbelievers.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r6.claim: Azwājan may be an accusative circumstantial qualifier of the pronoun in the verb, with the verb applying to them: some of them, or people among them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r6.anchor: ويجوزان ينصب حالا من هاء الضمير والفعل واقع على منهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r7.claim: Zahrat al-ḥayāt al-dunyā means the world's adornment and splendor.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r8.claim: Zahratan is accusative as blame, as an apposition to what they were given, or as an apposition to classes with an implied possessors of splendor.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r8.anchor: وانتصب على الذم وعلى ابداله محل به أو على ابداله من ازواجا على تقدير ذوي زهرة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r9.claim: One possible sense is that God tests them through it until their ingratitude makes them deserve punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r9.anchor: لنبلوهم حتى يستوجبوا العذاب لوجود الكفران منهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r10.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means that God will punish them in the afterlife because of it.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r11.claim: The Lord's provision can mean His reward, namely Paradise.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r12.claim: Alternatively, it means lawful, sufficient sustenance.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#2/r13.claim: The Lord's provision is better and more enduring than the worldly goods people received.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r1.claim: The phrase not to extend one's eyes toward what people enjoy was explained earlier in al-Ḥijr.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r2.claim: Azwājan is the object of mattaʿnā.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r2.anchor: مفعول ب«متعنا». و { زهرة } نصب على الحال.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r3.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses zahrah as an object in meaning because mattaʿnā means God made worldly life a flower for them, or supplies an omitted jaʿalnā.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r3.anchor: «زهرة» منصوبة بمعنى «متعنا» لأن معناه جعلنا لهم الحياة الدنيا زهرة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r4.claim: One view makes zahrah a substitute for the pronoun in bihi by its syntactic position, as in marartu bihi akhāka.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r4.anchor: وقيل: هي بدل من الهاء في «به» على الموضع

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r5.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r5.claim: Al-Farra parses zahrah as a circumstantial accusative governed by mattaʿnā, estimating that God gave them it as flower and adornment in worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r5.anchor: وأشار الفراء إلى نصبه على الحال والعامل فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r6.claim: Parsing zahrah as a cognate accusative, like ṣunʿ Allāh or waʿd Allāh, is possible but weak in the author's view.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن ينتصب على المصدر مثل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r7.claim: The best parse makes zahrah a circumstantial accusative, omitting tanwin at the lām; al-ḥayāh is genitive as a substitute for mā, giving the sense of the world's life in its flowering state.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r8.claim: Making zahrah a substitute for mā at its syntactic position does not work because linatnahum depends on mattaʿnā.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r8.anchor: ولا يحسن أن يكون «زهرة» بدلا من «ما» على الموضع

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r9.claim: Zahrah al-ḥayāh al-dunyā means the world's adornment in vegetation; zahrah with open vowels means a plant's flower, while ẓuhrah with ḍamma on zāy means a star.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r9.anchor: زهرة الحياة الدنيا } يعني زينتها بالنبات

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r10.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r10.claim: Isa ibn Umar reads zahrah with an open ha, by analogy with nahr and nahr.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r10.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر «زهرة» بفتح الهاء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r11.speaker: ابن عزيز
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r11.claim: Ibn Aziz notes that Banū Zuhra has a quiescent ha; zāhir describes a shining lamp, and flowers are named for their pleasing colors.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r11.anchor: وبنو زهرة بسكون الهاء قاله ابن عزيز

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r12.claim: The Prophet is described as azhar al-lawn, luminous in complexion; zāhir is used of anything shining and this is the finest color.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r12.anchor: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أزهر اللون أي نير اللون

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r13.claim: Linatnahum fīhi means to test them with worldly enjoyment, or to make it a temptation and misguidance for them.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r14.claim: Muhammad should assign no lasting worth to worldly adornment because it does not endure.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r14.anchor: ومعنى الآية: لا تجعل يا محمد لزهرة الدنيا وزنا، فإنه لا بقاء لها.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r15.claim: The command not to stretch one's eyes is stronger than a command merely not to look: prolonged gaze implies desire and greed, while looking need not.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r15.anchor: لأن الذي يمد بصره، إنما يحمله على ذلك حرص مقترن، والذي ينظر

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r16.speaker: أبو رافع
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132/r16.claim: Some attributed the occasion of revelation to Abu Rafi's report about a guest who came to the Prophet and his request for flour or a loan from a Jewish man.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r1.claim: The continuation of Abu Rafi's report says the Jew would sell or lend only with collateral; the Prophet sent his armor and said he would repay.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r1.anchor: نزل بنا ضيف ولم يلف عندنا بعض الذي يصلحه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r2.claim: The report says the verse was revealed to console the Prophet about worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r2.anchor: ونزلت الآية تعزية له عن الدنيا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects this as the occasion of revelation because the sura is Meccan while the story is Medinan, late in the Prophet's life, when he died with his armor pawned to a Jew.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r3.anchor: وهذا معترض أن يكون سببا لأن السورة مكية والقصة المذكورة مدنية

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya instead reads the verse in context: after rebuking failure to learn from past peoples and threatening delayed punishment, God tells the Prophet to discount their wealth and endure their words because it will end in disgrace.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r4.anchor: أن الآية متناسقة مع ما قبلها

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r5.claim: The author relates that the Prophet passed camels of Banu al-Mustaliq, covered in their dung and urine from fatness, covered himself with his garment, and moved on in response to the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r5.anchor: وكذلك ما روي عنه عليه السلام أنه مر بإبل بني المصطلق

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r6.claim: God's reward for patience and indifference to worldly life is better because it lasts while the world perishes.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r6.anchor: أي ثواب الله على الصبر وقلة المبالاة بالدنيا أولى لأنه يبقى والدنيا تفنى.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r7.claim: Another explanation takes God's provision to mean the lands and spoils He will open for believers.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r7.anchor: يعني بهذا الرزق ما يفتح الله على المؤمنين من البلاد والغنائم.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r10.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r10.claim: When Urwa ibn al-Zubayr saw reports about rulers, he hurried home, recited the verse through wa-abqā, called his household to prayer, and prayed.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r10.anchor: ويروى أن عروة بن الزبير رضي الله عنه كان إذا رأى شيئا من أخبار السلاطين وأحوالهم بادر إلى منزله فدخله

BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r1.claim: Some define extending the gaze as lingering in admiration and wishing to possess what one sees.
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم مد النظر تطويله وأن لا يكاد يرده استحسانا للمنظور إليه وإعجابا به وتمنيا أن له مثله

BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r2.claim: A brief glance followed by lowering the eyes is excused as unavoidable; the prohibition targets prolonged admiration, a common human impulse toward finery.
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r2.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن النظر الغير الممدود معفو عنه لأنه لا يمكن الاحتراز منه

BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r3.speaker: أبو رافع
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r3.claim: Al-Kāshifī transmits from Abū Rāfiʿ that, after a guest arrived and the Prophet lacked provisions, he sought flour on credit from a Jew and pledged his armor; the verse consoled him.

BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r4.claim: The root of matāʿ conveys extension and elevation; it can mean useful household goods or enjoyment extended over time.
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r4.anchor: وأصل المتوع الامتداد والارتفاع يقال متع النهار ومتع النبات ارتفع

BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r5.speaker: الكبير
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r5.claim: Al-Kabīr glosses mattaʿnā as delighting people through beautiful sights, stirring sounds, pleasant scents, clothing, and marriage.
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r5.anchor: وفي "الكبير" : ألذذنا به والامتاع الإلذاذ بما يدرك من المناظر الحسنة ويسمع من الأصوات المطربة

BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r6.claim: The groups enjoying these things are kinds of unbelievers, including polytheists and scripturalists such as Jews and Christians.
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r6.anchor: أي : أصنافا من الكفرة كالوثنى والكتابي من اليهود والنصارى

BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r7.claim: Zahrata is accusative under an understood verb indicated by mattaʿnā: God gave them worldly adornment, splendor, freshness, and beauty.
BURSEVI:v5p342#2/r7.anchor: منصوب بفعل يدل عليه متعنا أي : أعطينا زينة الدنيا وبهجتها ونضارتها وحسنها

BURSEVI:v5p343/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p343/r1.speaker: الواسطي
BURSEVI:v5p343/r1.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī reads the verse as consolation for the poor: even the best of creation was barred from admiring worldly life.
BURSEVI:v5p343/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي : هذه تسلية للفقراء وتعزية لهم حيث منع خير الخلق عن النظر إلى الدنيا على وجه الاستحسان

BURSEVI:v5p343/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p343/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p343/r2.claim: God tests people through what He gives; some respond to increased favors with greater disbelief and transgression and thus earn punishment.
BURSEVI:v5p343/r2.anchor: أي : لنعاملهم فيما أعطينا معاملة من نبتليهم حتى يستوجبوا العذاب

BURSEVI:v5p343/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p343/r3.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v5p343/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says not to admire the garments and mounts of the unjust, but to look for sin’s humiliation showing through their finery.
BURSEVI:v5p343/r3.anchor: حتى قال الحسن لا تنظروا إلى دقدقة هماليج الفسقة

BURSEVI:v5p343/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p343/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p343/r4.claim: Oppressors acquire displays to attract spectators, so admiring them serves their purpose and encourages further display.
BURSEVI:v5p343/r4.anchor: لأنهم اتخذوا هذه الأشياء لعيون النظارة فالناظر إليها محصل لغرضهم ومغر لهم على اتخاذها

BURSEVI:v5p343/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p343/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p343/r5.claim: A hadith calls worldly life sweet, green, and beautiful to the eye; the commentary says green evokes freshness and its quick disappearance like vegetation.
BURSEVI:v5p343/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث "إن الدنيا" أي : صورتها ومتاعها

BURSEVI:v5p343/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p343/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p343/r6.claim: The author cites Khujandī’s poem comparing worldly pleasures to honey whose bitterness and trouble exceed its sweetness.
BURSEVI:v5p343/r6.anchor: جهان وجمله لذاتش بزنبور عسل ماند كه شيرينيش بسيارست

BURSEVI:v5p343/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p343/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p343/r7.claim: The Mathnawī says that once a person sees through worldly life, it appears like carrion.
BURSEVI:v5p343/r7.anchor: هركه از ديدار بر خوردار شد اين جهان درشم او مردار شد

BURSEVI:v5p343/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p343/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p343/r8.claim: Ḥāfiẓ portrays the world as a crafty old woman who cloaks seduction in religion, deceives, and departs.
BURSEVI:v5p343/r8.anchor: ازره مرو بعشوه ديني كه اين عجوز مكاره مى نشيند ومحتاله مى رود

BURSEVI:v5p343/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p343/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p343/r9.claim: Ḥāfiẓ depicts the world as outwardly a beautiful bride whose suitor pays for marriage with his life.
BURSEVI:v5p343/r9.anchor: خوش عروسيست جهان ازره صورت ليكن هركه يوست بدو عمر خودش كابين داد

BURSEVI:v5p343/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p343/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p343/r10.claim: A hadith says God makes people successors in worldly life and watches how they act; their wealth is entrusted property over which they serve as agents.
BURSEVI:v5p343/r10.anchor: أي : جاعلكم خلفاء في الدنيا يعني أن أموالكم ليست هي في الحقيقة لكم

BURSEVI:v5p343/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p343/r11.speaker: عيسى بن مريم
BURSEVI:v5p343/r11.claim: Jesus warns people not to make worldly life their lord, lest it make them its slaves.
BURSEVI:v5p343/r11.anchor: وعن عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام لا تتخذوا الدنيا ربا فتتخذكم لها عبيدا

BURSEVI:v5p343/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p343/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p343/r12.claim: The author follows al-Tawīlāt al-Najmiyya in reading the two eyes as bodily sight and inner vision, with divine vision admitting no association.
BURSEVI:v5p343/r12.anchor: أي عيني البصر والبصيرة وهما عين الرأس وعين القلب

BURSEVI:v5p343/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p343/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p343/r13.claim: The Najmī reading extends the allusion to both worldly and afterlife enjoyments, calling for cleansing outer and inner sight of attachment to either.
BURSEVI:v5p343/r13.anchor: اغسل عيني ظاهرك وباطنك بماء العزة عن وصمة رؤية الدنيا والآخرة

BURSEVI:v5p343/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p343/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p343/r14.claim: In the inward reading, enjoyment of either abode can distract people from attaining the perfection of beholding divine beauty.
BURSEVI:v5p343/r14.anchor: وإنما متعنا أهل الدارين بهما عزة لحضرة جلالنا

BURSEVI:v5p344/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344/r1.speaker: الشبلي
BURSEVI:v5p344/r1.claim: When al-Shiblī heard the verse about Paradise’s people being occupied, he gasped that they did not know whose presence occupied them.
BURSEVI:v5p344/r1.anchor: قيل : قرىء عند الشبلي قدس سره

BURSEVI:v5p344/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344/r2.claim: The Prophet’s provision may mean afterlife reward stored for him or modest sufficiency received with obedience.
BURSEVI:v5p344/r2.anchor: أي : ما ادخر لك في الآخرة من الثواب أو ما أوتيته من يسير الكفاية

BURSEVI:v5p344/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344/r3.claim: Rizq can mean a worldly or otherworldly gift, an allotted share, or food that reaches and nourishes the body.
BURSEVI:v5p344/r3.anchor: والرزق يقال للعطاء دنيويا كان أو أخرويا وللنصيب تارة ولما يوصل إلى الجوف ويتغذى به تارة

BURSEVI:v5p344/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344/r4.claim: The provision is better because it is the highest object of competition and is safe from worldly harm.
BURSEVI:v5p344/r4.anchor: لأنه مع كونه في نفسه أجل ما يتنافس فيه المتنافسون مأمون الغائلة

BURSEVI:v5p344/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344/r5.claim: It is more enduring because it will not end.

BURSEVI:v5p344/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344/r6.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p344/r6.claim: Al-Kāshifī cites Kashf al-Asrār: zahrah means flower; the dinar is called a flower because its freshness lasts only briefly before withering.
BURSEVI:v5p344/r6.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (در كشف الاسرار آورده كه زهر درلغت شكوفه است

BURSEVI:v5p344/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344/r7.claim: The author cites Saʿdī praising contentment with little: worldly sweetness is not worth its sting, and appetite degrades those who indulge it.
BURSEVI:v5p344/r7.anchor: كر آزاده برزمين خسب وبس مكن بهرفانى زمين بوس كس نيرزد عسل جان من زخم نيش

BURSEVI:v5p344/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344/r8.claim: The most valuable provision nourishes the holy spirit with knowledge, wisdom, primordial effusion, and divine manifestation.
BURSEVI:v5p344/r8.anchor: ثم إن الرزق المعتبر غاية الاعتبار ما صار غذاء للروح القدسي من العلم والحكمة والفيض الأزلي والتجلي

BURSEVI:v5p344/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344/r9.claim: The Mathnawī contrasts bread with wisdom and says spiritual nourishment opens the inner mouth to mysteries.
BURSEVI:v5p344/r9.anchor: فهم نان كردى نه حكمت اى رهى زانكه حق كفت كلوا من رزقه
